title: The Story of the Two Viziers, Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri and Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri

paragraphs.en: I heard that long ago, in Egypt, there ruled a just and powerful king who associated with scholars and cared for the poor. He had a wise and influential vizier named Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri, an old man of great experience. His two sons, Shams al-Din Muhammad and Nur al-Din Ali, were equally beautiful but the younger surpassed his elder in grace.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说很久以前，在埃及有一位公正而强大的国王，他与学者为伍，关心贫民。这位国王手下有一位智者和有影响力的宰相，名叫努尔丁·阿里·米斯里，是一位饱经风霜的老人。他的两个儿子，沙姆斯丁·穆罕默德和努尔丁·阿里，同样英俊，但 younger 的弟弟在风度上更胜一筹。

paragraphs.en: Upon their father's death, the king mourned him deeply and appointed both sons as joint viziers. They honored this with a month-long period of mourning before taking up their duties. Each son served for a week at a time, accompanying the king on journeys and living together in one house.
paragraphs.zh: 两位儿子的父亲去世后，国王深感哀悼，并任命他们为共治宰相。为了表达对父亲的怀念，他们在正式履职前度过了一个月的守丧期。随后，两人轮流每周一上任，陪同国王出行，并共同居住在一处宅邸中。

paragraphs.en: Their unity was unwavering.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的团结坚如磐石。

paragraphs.en: One night before his journey with the king, the elder brother proposed to his younger sibling Nur al-Din. He suggested they marry two sisters on the same day and consummate their marriages on the same night. Upon returning from his trip, they would seek suitable brides for their wives.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个夜晚，大哥在陪同国王出行前向弟弟努尔·阿丁提议。他建议两人在同一天娶两位姐妹为妻，并在同一夜完婚。等他从旅行归来后，再分别为他们的妻子寻觅合适的伴侣。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din agreed but suggested waiting until after the journey. The elder brother, Shams al-Din, proposed a scenario: if both couples conceived on their wedding night and gave birth to a boy and a girl respectively on the same day, he asked whether Nur al-Din would marry his son to his daughter.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁同意了，但建议等到旅行结束后再说。年长的哥哥沙姆斯丁提出一个设想：如果两对夫妇都在洞房花烛夜怀上了孩子，并且分别在同一天生下一个男孩和一个女孩，他问努尔丁是否愿意将自己的儿子娶给他的女儿。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din agreed but inquired about the dowry. Shams al-Din demanded at least three thousand dinars, three orchards, and three farms, plus an unspecified amount. Nur al-Din questioned such a high dowry, emphasizing their brotherhood and shared responsibilities as viziers.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁同意了，但还是询问了嫁妆的问题。沙姆斯丁要求至少三千第纳尔、三处果园和三块农田，外加一笔未定的数目。努尔丁对如此高的嫁妆表示质疑，强调他们作为同僚和共事兄弟的责任与义务。

paragraphs.en: He suggested no dowry for his son to marry Shams al-Din's daughter.
paragraphs.zh: 他提议不为儿子提供嫁妆，打算让他的儿子娶沙姆斯丁的女儿。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din quoted a verse: "When one postpones the favor for a day, The wise man knows that he has answered, 'Nay.'"
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁引用了一句诗：“倘若好事被拖延至明日，智者已知他回答的是‘不’。”

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din said, "Enough of your comments. You lack understanding and wisdom. I will never marry my daughter to your son, not even for his weight in gold."
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁说道：“住口吧，你的这些话我听够了。你缺乏理解和智慧。我绝不会把女儿嫁给你的儿子，哪怕他值金山银山我也不会答应。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din became furious but hid his anger. Shams al-Din declared he would vindicate his honor upon returning from a journey.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁气得脸色铁青，却强忍怒火。沙姆斯丁则宣称，等他从旅行中归来，一定要为自己洗清冤屈。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din's rage grew as they prepared for the king’s morning departure to the pyramids with Shams al-Din. That night, Nur al-Din filled a saddlebag with gold and recalled his brother's insults. He recited verses about travel and toil:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁的怒火随着国王和沙姆斯丁准备清晨启程前往金字塔而愈发强烈。当晚，努尔·丁在鞍袋里装满了金币，并回想起了他哥哥的侮辱。他吟诵起关于旅行与劳苦的诗句：

paragraphs.en: Travel, and new friends will succeed the ones you lost, And toil, for life’s sweets do through toil come. To stay wins you no honor nor from exile saves; Set out to roam the world and leave your home.
paragraphs.zh: 旅行吧，失去的朋友将会被新朋友取代， 努力吧，生活的甜蜜只有通过努力才能获得。 留在此地既不能赢得荣誉，也无法摆脱流放； 启程周游世界，离开你的家园。

paragraphs.en: Water stagnant turns and stinks but tastes so sweet when it flows, And if the sun stood still, both Arabs and barbarians would tire of its light. If the full moon did not wane and set, no eyes would mark its rising. In a lair, the lion stays; in the bow, the dart hits not the mark.
paragraphs.zh: 静止的水变得污浊而发出恶臭，但一旦流动起来却如此甘甜；若太阳停在空中，无论是阿拉伯人还是异族人都会厌倦它的光芒。如果满月永不亏缺和落下，人们也不会注意到它的升起。洞穴中，狮子安眠；弓弦一松，箭矢便无法命中目标。

paragraphs.en: Deep in the mine, gold dust is merely dust, And in its native ground, fuel aloewood.
paragraphs.zh: 在矿井深处，黄金尘仅是尘埃， 在故土之中，燃料不过为沉香。

paragraphs.en: Gold, when extracted, grows much in demand, And when exported, aloe fetches gold.
paragraphs.zh: 提炼出的黄金需求大增，而出口芦荟则能换回大量黄金。

paragraphs.en: After reciting some verses, the vizier ordered one of his pages to saddle his Arabian she-mule. The animal was particularly fine, with dappled gray skin, sharp ears like reed pens, and sturdy legs. He instructed the page to prepare her fully, including saddlebags covered in silk carpeting.
paragraphs.zh: 念了几首诗后， vizier 命令其中一个侍从为他的阿拉伯母驴鞴鞍。这头驴格外俊美，皮毛斑驳灰白，耳朵尖如芦管笔，四肢健壮。他吩咐侍从不仅要备好鞍具，还要在鞍垫上铺上丝绸地毯。

paragraphs.en: With provisions in hand, he mounted the she-mule and left Cairo for a brief excursion near Qalyubiya.
paragraphs.zh: 拿着干粮，他骑上母驴，前往开罗附近的卡利伯亚地区进行短暂的郊游。

paragraphs.en: At midday, he arrived at Bilbis, where he rested and ate. Afterward, he took food and forage for his she-mule before continuing into the desert. By nightfall, they reached al-Sa’idiya, where he spent the night at the post station.
paragraphs.zh: 中午时分，他抵达比尔比斯城，在那里休息并用餐。随后，他为自己的母驼准备了食物和饲料，继续向沙漠深处进发。夜幕降临之际，他们终于到达萨伊迪亚，当晚便在驿站过夜。

paragraphs.en: He walked the she-mule a few times, gave her fodder, then lay down on a carpeted seat, still angry. Determined to continue, he vowed, "By God, I will ride even if it takes me as far as Baghdad."
paragraphs.zh: 他几次牵着母驴散步，喂了它一些饲料，然后坐在一张地毯垫子上躺下，依然怒气未消。决心继续行动，他发誓道：“凭真主起誓，我就是走到巴格达也要骑上去。”

paragraphs.en: The next morning, he resumed his journey and met a courier. They rode together, stopping whenever the courier did. Eventually, they reached Basra safely.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，他继续上路，并遇到了一名信使。两人并辔而行，每当信使停歇他们也随之驻马。最终，他们安全抵达了巴士拉。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri was traveling when he met Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri on the road. The vizier noticed Nur al-Din's handsome appearance and polite demeanor, and approached him to inquire about his situation.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·阿勒·密斯里正在旅行，途中遇到了巴德尔丁·哈桑·阿勒·巴斯里。见努尔丁仪表堂堂且举止文雅，宰相便上前询问他的情况。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din explained that he had quarreled with his family and vowed not to return until he had visited all the world’s countries, even if it meant risking his life. Upon hearing this, Badr al-Din expressed concern for Nur al-Din's safety and suggested he stay in Basra instead.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁解释说，他与家人发生了争执，并发誓除非游览了世界上所有的国家，否则不会回家，即使这意味着要冒生命危险。听到这话，巴德·丁表达了对努尔·丁安全的担忧，并建议他在巴士拉待下来。

paragraphs.en: Moved by Nur al-Din's story, Badr al-Din invited him home and treated him kindly. He then proposed that Nur al-Din marry his daughter, who was equally beautiful. If they were to wed, Badr al-Din would petition the king to make Nur al-Din vizier in his place, allowing him to retire.
paragraphs.zh: 被努尔·阿丁的故事打动，巴德尔·阿丁邀请他回家，并以友好的态度款待。随后，巴德尔·阿丁提议让努尔·阿丁娶他的女儿为妻，而这位女儿同样美丽。如果两人成婚，巴德尔·阿丁将向国王请求让努尔·阿丁接替自己的职位担任 vizier，从而让他得以退休。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din considered for a moment before agreeing. Overjoyed, Badr al-Din quickly prepared a feast and arranged for their wedding. He invited prominent Basran families and gathered friends to witness the union of the two young men.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁沉思了一会儿才答应。巴德·丁喜出望外，迅速安排了一场盛宴，并为他们的婚礼做了准备。他邀请了基斯兰的名门望族，并召集了许多朋友来见证这两名年轻人的结合。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Ja’far spoke to the caliph. The prominent men of Basra congratulated the vizier. Witnesses arrived, tables were set for a banquet, guests ate until satisfied, and enjoyed sweets.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，贾法尔与哈里发进行了交谈。巴士拉的重要人物向 vizier 马利克·丁·巴兹瑞表示了祝贺。证人到场，摆开了宴席，宾客们吃饱喝足后还品尝了美味的甜点。

paragraphs.en: Servants cleared the tables as witnesses signed the marriage contract.
paragraphs.zh: 仆人们正清理桌子，见证人则在婚约文书上签字。

paragraphs.en: Then the vizier ordered his servants to prepare Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri for the bath. They brought him royal attire, towels, incense, and other necessities. After bathing, Nur al-Din returned, looking radiant like the moon or sun.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，首相吩咐仆人为努尔·阿丁·阿里·米斯里准备沐浴。他们给他带来了皇家的服饰、毛巾、香料以及其他必需品。洗完澡后，努尔·阿丁焕然一新，光彩照人，犹如明月或旭日。

paragraphs.en: He entered his father-in-law's presence, kissed his hand, and was greeted with respect.
paragraphs.zh: 他走进岳父的住所，吻了吻对方的手，受到了应有的尊敬。

paragraphs.en: The vizier asked, "Son, tell me why you left your family and how they allowed it. Be truthful." Nur al-Din replied, "O great Vizier, I am not of humble origin; my father was a vizier.
paragraphs.zh: vizier问道：“儿子，你为何离开家庭，他们又是如何允许的？说实话。”努尔·阿德丁回答说：“伟大的 vizier ，我出身并不卑微；我的父亲也曾是 vizier 。

paragraphs.en: After he died, disputes arose between myself and my brother. You were kind enough to marry me to your daughter."
paragraphs.zh: 他去世后，我和弟弟之间产生了争执。你够仗义，把女儿嫁给了我。”

paragraphs.en: The vizier was amazed. Smiling, he said, "My son, you quarreled even before marriage! Tomorrow, I will take you to the king.
paragraphs.zh: 宰相惊讶不已，微笑着说道：“我的儿子，你们竟然在婚前就争吵不休！明天我带你去见国王。”

paragraphs.en: May God grant you every blessing."
paragraphs.zh: 愿真主赐予你一切福祉。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din married in Basra on the same night his brother Shams al-Din married a girl in Egypt.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁在巴士拉迎娶新娘，当天他的弟弟沙姆斯·丁在埃及也成婚了。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din traveled with the Egyptian king for a month before returning home. Upon his arrival, he could not find Nur al-Din and asked his servants. They told him that Nur al-Din had left early and was gone without a trace.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁随埃及国王同行一个月后才返回家中。一到家，他就四处打听努尔丁的下落，问起仆人们。仆人告诉他，努尔丁早就离开了，连一点踪迹都没有留下。

paragraphs.en: Feeling deeply troubled by the loss of his brother, Shams al-Din vowed to search for Nur al-Din. He sent couriers to Aleppo but received no news about him. Desperate, he concluded, "There is no power or strength except in God."
paragraphs.zh: 深感失去哥哥萨姆斯·丁的痛苦，努尔·丁·阿里决心寻找他。他派人去阿勒颇打听消息，却一无所获。绝望之下，他脱口而出：“除了上帝，人类没有任何力量和依靠。”

paragraphs.en: Realizing his mistake, he reflected on their quarrel over the marriage.
paragraphs.zh: 意识到自己的错误，他回想起两人因婚事而起的争执。

paragraphs.en: Some time later, God willed that Shams al-Din should marry the daughter of a Cairo merchant on the same day his brother did in Basra. Consequently, both brothers drew up their marriage contracts and consummated their marriages on the same night—one in Cairo and one in Basra.
paragraphs.zh: 不久之后，上帝安排沙姆斯丁娶开罗某商人的女儿，与他在巴士拉的兄弟同一天完婚。因此，两兄弟在同一天晚上分别在开罗和巴士拉完成了婚礼手续并举行了洞房花烛夜。

paragraphs.en: In Egypt, Shams al-Din's wife gave birth to a girl. In Basra, Nur al-Din Ali's wife bore a son who was exceptionally beautiful. His neck was as white as marble, his brow radiant, and his cheeks rosy.
paragraphs.zh: 在埃及，沙姆斯·丁的妻子生下一个女儿。而在巴士拉，努尔·丁·阿里妻子产下一子，异常俊美。他的脖子白皙如玉，眉宇间光彩照人，脸颊红润可爱。

paragraphs.en: On his right cheek, there was a mole like ambergris.
paragraphs.zh: 在他的右脸颊上，有一颗像琥珀一样的痦子。

paragraphs.en: This boy was so graceful that he outshone the moon and sun. He was described by poets as:
paragraphs.zh: 这个男孩举止优雅，光芒甚至超过了明月和太阳。诗人形容他：

paragraphs.en: Here is a slender youth whose hair and face All mortals envelope with light and gloom. Mark on his cheek the mark of charm and grace, A dark spot on a red anemone.
paragraphs.zh: 这是一个身材修长的青年，他的头发和面容在凡人的眼中既沐浴着光芒也笼罩着阴影。在他的脸颊上，有着魅力与优雅的印记，犹如一朵红紫扇贝上的深色斑点。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali named him Badr al-Din Hasan, and his grandfather, the Basra vizier, rejoiced. He threw banquets in honor of the child and distributed gifts fit for kings.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里给他起名哈桑·班达尔丁，他的祖父——巴士拉的首相——听闻此事后欣喜若狂。他特地举办盛宴庆祝，并向宾客们赠送了足以让国王都眼热的礼物。

paragraphs.en: One day, Nur al-Din Ali, the Basra vizier, accompanied his brother to the king. When he entered, he kissed the ground and recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，纳尔丁·阿里·阿勒·米斯里陪他的哥哥觐见国王。进入大殿后，他跪吻地面，并吟诵了这几行诗句：

paragraphs.en: May you long live in glory, night and day, And may eternal bliss attend your way. He was a cultivated, intelligent, generous, and gentle man.
paragraphs.zh: 但愿你日夜荣耀长存，愿永恒的幸福伴随你的征途。他是一位博学、聪慧、慷慨且温和的人。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din was promoted to vizier after his father-in-law's recommendation. The king praised Nur al-Din and granted him a robe of honor, a she-mule, and stipends. Both Nur al-Din and his father-in-law rejoiced at their good fortune.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁在岳父的推荐下晋升为首相，国王对努尔·丁赞赏有加，并赐给他一件荣典袍、一匹母驴以及一些津贴。努尔·丁和他的岳父都为这份好运感到欣喜。

paragraphs.en: The next day, Nur al-Din took the vizier’s seat and performed his duties with ease, earning the king's favor. He returned home content as the vizier of Basra.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，努尔·阿丁坐上了宰相的位置，履职轻松自如，赢得了国王的青睐。作为巴士拉的宰相，他满心欢喜地回到了家中。

paragraphs.en: Years passed, and Nur al-Din's son Badr al-Din grew into a charming child. At four years old, he inherited his grandfather's wealth upon his death. As Badr al-Din thrived, Nur al-Din enrolled him in school at seven, instructing the tutor to educate and train the boy well.
paragraphs.zh: 几年过去，努尔·阿丁的儿子巴德尔·阿丁成长为一个惹人喜爱的孩子。四岁那年，他在祖父去世后继承了巨额财富。随着巴德尔·阿丁的成长，努尔·阿丁在七岁时将他送入学堂，叮嘱老师要对他好好教育和培养。

paragraphs.en: In school, Badr al-Din excelled, known for his intelligence and good manners. For two years, he studied diligently under his tutor's guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 在学堂里，巴德尔丁表现优异，以其聪慧和良好的举止而闻名。在他的导师指导下，他勤奋学习了两年之久。

paragraphs.en: By age twelve, Badr al-Din had mastered reading, writing, calligraphy, mathematics, and jurisprudence. His father, Nur al-Din Ali, dressed him in fine clothes and took him through the city on a she-mule. The people praised his beauty and charm, praying for both him and his father.
paragraphs.zh: 到十二岁的时候，巴德尔丁已经掌握了阅读、书写、书法、数学和法学。他的父亲努尔丁阿里给他穿上了华贵的衣裳，并骑着母驴带他游历全城。人们赞美他的英俊与魅力，为他和他的父亲祈祷。

paragraphs.en: From then on, Badr rode with his father daily, drawing admiration wherever they went.
paragraphs.zh: 从那以后，巴德每天都会随父亲出行，无论走到哪里都引来人们的钦佩。

paragraphs.en: When he turned twenty, Nur al-Din Ali, now feeble, summoned his son to impart wisdom. He shared five admonitions before recalling their home and weeping over the separation from loved ones and distant lands. His passion led him to recite these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 二十岁那年，如今已身体虚弱的努尔丁·阿里召来儿子，传授智慧。他先告诫了五条忠言，然后忆起往昔家园，不禁泪流满面，思念亲人和远方的土地。他的情感激昂，吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: I blame you and proclaim my ardent love.
paragraphs.zh: 我责怪你，并且表白我的深情。

paragraphs.en: After reciting verses and stopping his tears, he addressed his son. "Before I give you advice, know that I left my brother without consent, as it was foreordained." He wrote a letter detailing their past, his rise to vizier in Basra, and the date of his marriage.
paragraphs.zh: 诵读完经文，止住了泪水后，他转向儿子说道：“在我给你忠告之前，要知道我离开哥哥并非出于自愿，这是命中注定的。”随后，他写了一封信，详细记述了他们过去的种种，自己在巴士拉晋升为首相的经历，以及成婚的具体日期。

paragraphs.en: Sealing the scroll, he said, "Keep this with you always."
paragraphs.zh: 封好信件，他说道：“你一直要把它带在身边。”

paragraphs.en: Later, his father opened his eyes and gave him two pieces of advice. First, do not associate with anyone; isolation ensures safety. He quoted a poet: "There is no true friend in adversity."
paragraphs.zh: 后来，他父亲睁开眼睛，给他提出了两条建议。首先，不要与任何人交往；隔离能确保安全。他引用了一位诗人的诗句：“患难之中没有真正的朋友。”

paragraphs.en: Second, avoid oppressing others to prevent fortune's retribution. The poet advised, "Be merciful, for mercy will be shown."
paragraphs.zh: 其次，不要欺压他人以避免逆境的报复。诗人劝告说：“施以仁慈，因为仁慈终将得到回报。”

paragraphs.en: Finally, he urged his son to hold his tongue and preserve silence. Quoting another poem, he said, "Silence is safe; do not babble."
paragraphs.zh: 最后，他催促儿子闭上嘴巴，保持沉默。引用另一首诗，他说：“沉默是金，莫要多言。”

paragraphs.en: Fourth, my son, avoid wine as it clouds your judgment. Beware, for it leads to ruin. I have heard a poet say: "I renounced wine and joined its detractors; it misleads men and opens all evil doors."
paragraphs.zh: 第四，我的儿子，你要避开酒，因为它会模糊你的判断。小心为妙，因为酒会导致败坏。我曾听一位诗人说过：“我戒了酒，并加入了反对它的人；它误导世人，开启了所有邪恶之门。”

paragraphs.en: Lastly, protect your wealth, for it can shield you. Do not squander it or rely on the lowly. A poet warns: "When my wealth wanes, friends vanish; when it grows, they gather around."
paragraphs.zh: 最后，保护好你的财富，因为财富可以为你遮风挡雨。不要挥霍它，也不要依赖那些微不足道的人。一位诗人警告说：“当我囊中羞涩时，朋友都离我而去；当我腰缠万贯时，他们又纷纷围拢过来。”

paragraphs.en: Follow this advice.
paragraphs.zh: 采纳这条建议吧。

paragraphs.en: He spoke until his last breath. Then incense was burned and he was laid to rest.
paragraphs.zh: 他直到最后一息都在说话。随后点燃了香料，将他安葬。

paragraphs.en: Morning came for Shahrazad, who fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, that was a captivating tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait till tomorrow night if I live!"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳兹德说道：“姐姐，那真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“如果我还活着，就等明晚吧！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged, "Tell us more." Shahrazad agreed: "With pleasure."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳兹达催促道：“给我们讲更多吧。”莎赫拉兹德应允了：“我很乐意。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far then spoke to the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔随后对哈里发说道。

paragraphs.en: After Nur al-Din Ali's death, his son Badr al-Din mourned for two months. When the king grew angry, he appointed one of his chamberlains as vizier and ordered him to seize Nur al-Din Ali’s assets. The new vizier, accompanied by guards and clerks, went to Nur al-Din Ali's house.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁·阿里去世后，他的儿子巴德尔·丁哀悼了两个月。国王生气之后，任命了一位近臣为首相，并命令他接管努尔·丁·阿里的财产。新任首相带着卫兵和书记官前往努尔·丁·阿里的住所。

paragraphs.en: A Mamluk who had served under Nur al-Din Ali heard the order and rushed to Badr al-Din Hasan. Finding him at his gate, the Mamluk urged him to flee, warning that the king was angry and would arrest him. Terrified, Badr al-Din asked if he could go inside first.
paragraphs.zh: 一名曾在努尔·丁·阿里手下服役的马穆鲁克听到命令后，急忙赶到巴德尔·丁·哈桑身边。他发现巴德尔·丁站在门口，便催促他赶快逃走，警告说国王正怒气冲冲，准备逮捕他。巴德尔·丁吓得浑身发抖，连忙问是否可以先进屋再说。

paragraphs.en: The Mamluk insisted he leave immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 马穆鲁克坚持要他立刻离开。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din put on his shoes, covered his head with his robe’s hem, and fled in confusion. He recited verses about saving oneself from injustice:
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁穿上鞋子，用袍子的下摆蒙住头，慌乱地逃走了。他念起了逃避不公的诗句：

paragraphs.en: "If you suffer injustice, save yourself, And leave the house behind to mourn its builder. Your country you'll replace by another, But for yourself you'll find no other self."
paragraphs.zh: “如果你蒙受不公，自救为上， 抛下这座宅第，哀悼它的主人。 你可换一个国家，却找不到另一个自我。”

paragraphs.en: He left the hem of his robe hanging as he walked among the tombs, reciting more lines:
paragraphs.zh: 他披着长袍，在墓地间缓步而行，口中念诵着更多的诗句，长袍的下摆随风轻轻飘动。

paragraphs.en: "You who with the dew and stars Do with face so radiant vie, May your fortune stay the same And your glory ever high."
paragraphs.zh: “你那面若朝霞、星辰璀璨，愿你的命运恒久不变，荣耀长存不衰。”

paragraphs.en: Dinarzad urged Shahrazad to continue her story. She obliged:
paragraphs.zh: 迪纳兹达催促沙赫拉兹德继续讲述她的故事。沙赫拉兹德应允了：

paragraphs.en: One night, Badr al-Din met a Jew on his way to the city. The Jew greeted him warmly, asking where he was heading as it was late. Badr al-Din explained that he had seen his father in a dream and wanted to visit before nightfall.
paragraphs.zh: 一天晚上，巴德尔丁在前往城市的路上遇到了一个犹太人。那犹太人热情地向他问好，并询问这么晚了他还去哪儿。巴德尔丁解释说他在梦中见到了父亲，想趁夜色未深前去探望。

paragraphs.en: The Jew, eager to secure the cargo of arriving ships, offered to buy the first ship's goods for a thousand dinars. After weighing out the money, they wrote an agreement: Badr al-Din sold the cargo to Isaac the Jew for that sum. The Jew then left, and Badr al-Din continued his journey.
paragraphs.zh: 犹太人急于购得即将到港的船只货物，提出以一千第纳尔买下第一艘船上的商品。双方算清了钱款后，写下了合约：巴德尔丁将这批货物卖给了犹太人伊萨克。随后，犹太人离开了，而巴德尔丁则继续他的旅程。

paragraphs.en: Upon reaching his father’s tomb, Badr al-Din wept and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 抵达父亲的墓前，巴德尔·丁泪流满面，吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: Since you left me, home is no longer home, Nor is the neighbor neighbor, since you went away. The friend who kept me company Is not the friend I knew, nor is the day bright day. For they will never shine again in desolation.
paragraphs.zh: 自从你离开以后 家已不再似从前，邻人亦非旧时情 昔日相伴的朋友 如今已非往日模样，晴天也不再明亮 因为那些光辉再也不会在荒凉中闪耀

paragraphs.en: In gloomy darkness, every field and plain.
paragraphs.zh: 在阴沉的黑暗中，每一处田野和平原。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan wept at his father’s tomb for an hour, feeling lost and uncertain about his future. As he slept there, his head rolled off, and he lay on his back against the tomb.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁·哈桑在他的父亲墓前痛哭了一个小时，对未来感到迷茫和不确定。他昏睡过去时，头滚落在一边，仰面躺在墓碑旁。

paragraphs.en: That night, a demon, who haunted the cemetery by day and fled to another at night, saw a fully dressed man lying sprawled. Intrigued by his beauty, the demon approached.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，一个白日出没墓地、夜晚则逃往别处的妖魔看见一个衣着齐全却横躺在那里的男子。出于对其美貌的好奇，妖魔走了过去。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Shahrazad paused her story as dawn approached. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an engaging tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to tell you then."
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，当黎明临近时，沙赫拉兹停下了故事。迪纳兹说道：“姐姐，真是引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹回答道：“等到明天晚上再听吧；我还有很多精彩的故事要告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: Ja'far told the caliph a story.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉兹朵开始讲述：贾法尔向哈里发讲了一个故事。

paragraphs.en: The demon admired Hasan al-Basri's beauty as he slept. Rising to the heavens, he encountered a she-demon who agreed to accompany him to a cemetery. There, the demon asked if Hasan was more beautiful than any man she had seen.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔在哈桑·阿巴斯入睡时被他的美貌所吸引，腾空而起，途中遇到了一只雌性恶魔，同意与他一同前往一处墓地。到达后，恶魔问哈桑是否比她见过的任何男人都更漂亮。

paragraphs.en: The she-demon then revealed an extraordinary tale: in Cairo, there was a vizier named Shams al-Din Muhammad with a daughter resembling Badr al-Din. The king of Egypt heard of her beauty and demanded her hand in marriage from the vizier.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，女妖讲述了一个令人惊讶的故事：在开罗，有一位名为沙姆斯丁·穆罕默德的宰相，他的女儿长得与巴德尔丁非常相似。埃及国王听说了她的美貌，便向宰相提出要迎娶她为妻。

paragraphs.en: The vizier explained that his brother Nur al-Din had disappeared twenty years ago after discussing marriage. Recently, he learned that Nur al-Din had died in Basra, leaving behind a son. The vizier argued that his daughter was reserved for her cousin and suggested other women were available to the king.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 解释说，二十年前他的兄弟努尔·丁在讨论婚事时突然失踪。最近他得知努尔·丁死于巴士拉，并留下了一个儿子。vizier 坚持认为他的女儿应该嫁给堂兄，并建议国王可以考虑其他女性。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing this, the king became angry.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，国王怒气冲天。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: O King, Ja’far told the caliph that the king was furious with Shams al-Din's excuse for his daughter. The king vowed to marry her to no one but a lowly servant and chose a hunchbacked groom. He ordered the vizier to draft a marriage contract between his daughter and this groom on the spot, promising to parade him in procession that night.
paragraphs.zh: 国王陛下，贾法尔告诉哈里发，国王对沙姆斯丁为女儿提出的借口极为愤怒。国王誓言一定要将女儿嫁给一个卑微的仆人，并且选中了一个驼背的新郎。他命令 vizier 立刻起草一份婚约，当晚还要在游行中展示这位新郎。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then revealed that she had left the princes and their Mamluks waiting outside with lit candles for the groom's arrival. Meanwhile, her father kept the vizier’s daughter under guard until the hunchback could marry her. The demon argued with the she-demon over who was more beautiful, but agreed to carry Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri in his sleep to the girl.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫札德随后透露，她已经让王子和他们的马穆鲁克侍卫在门外等候，手中拿着点燃的蜡烛等待新郎的到来。与此同时，她的父亲则将 vizier 的女儿关押起来，直到驼背能够娶她为妻。恶魔与雌魔争论谁更美丽，但最终同意在夜间睡梦中背着 Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri 前往那女孩的住所。

paragraphs.en: The demon and she-demon flew up, landing at Cairo's gate where they placed Badr al-Din on a bench and woke him.
paragraphs.zh: 那恶魔和雌魔腾空而起，落在开罗城门处，将巴德尔·丁放在一张长凳上，把他唤醒了。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din woke in an unfamiliar city. The demon jabbed him awake, handed a thick candle, and instructed: "Go to the bath, mingle with Mamluks and people until you reach the wedding hall. Enter as if you're a candle bearer, stand by the hunchbacked groom, and give gold to those who approach, trusting in God's will."
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁在一座陌生的城市中醒来。恶魔一把将他唤醒，递给他一支粗大的蜡烛，并吩咐道：“去澡堂，与马穆鲁克人和其他人混熟，直到你到达婚礼大厅。进去时像一名执烛者一样自然，站在驼背的新郎身边，遇到接近的人就给他们黄金，相信上帝的意愿。”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din rose, lit the candle, and followed the instructions.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁站起身，点燃蜡烛，然后照着指示做了。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Shahrazad paused her tale, and Dinarzad urged: "Sister, what an engaging story!" Shahrazad replied: "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: Meanwhile, 莎赫拉兹德暂停了故事，丁达尔兹催促道：“姐姐，多精彩的故事啊！”莎赫拉兹德回答说：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等到明天晚上吧。"

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began anew: Ja’far told the caliph about Badr al-Din's journey.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德又开始了她的讲述：贾法尔向哈里发讲述了巴德尔丁的旅程。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan walked through the procession, throwing gold into the tambourines of singing women. His beauty and generosity amazed everyone. Upon reaching his uncle's vizier palace, the doormen blocked the crowd but let in the singing women who insisted on Hasan entering with them.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁·哈桑漫步在行进的队伍中，将金币抛向唱歌女子手中的鼓。他的美貌与慷慨让众人惊叹不已。当他抵达叔叔的首相府邸时，守门人挡住了人群，但放过了坚持要与哈桑一同进入的唱歌女子。

paragraphs.en: They brought him to the wedding hall where he was seated next to a hunchback.
paragraphs.zh: 他们把他带到了婚宴大厅，在那里他坐在一个驼背人的旁边。

paragraphs.en: Princes' wives, viziers' spouses, chamberlains, and deputies lined up in two rows, each holding a lit candle. The women were captivated by Hasan's beauty; his face shone like the moon, and his body swayed gracefully. They loved him even more when he showered them with money.
paragraphs.zh: 王公贵妇、宰相夫人、内侍和副使排成两列，每人手中拿着一支点燃的蜡烛。这些妇女被哈桑的英俊所吸引；他的脸庞皎洁如月，身姿轻盈优雅。当他向她们倾囊相赠时，她们对他的喜爱更是有增无减。

paragraphs.en: The hunchback, dressed in a brocaded robe and double turban, sat curled up like a ball, resembling a toy rather than a man. The women cursed the king for bringing this about, wishing Hasan were lying in his lap instead of the hunchback.
paragraphs.zh: 驼背穿着绣花长袍，戴着双层头巾，蜷缩成一团，看起来像一个玩偶而不是男人。女人们咒骂国王带来了这样的结果，恨不得哈桑此刻躺在她们的怀里，而不是那个驼背身上。

paragraphs.en: The women mocked the hunchback while praising Badr al-Din Hasan. As morning approached, Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad urged her sister to continue the story if she was spared.
paragraphs.zh: 驼背的仆人遭到女人们的嘲笑，而巴德尔·丁·哈桑则受到了赞扬。黎明渐渐临近，沙赫拉兹阿德沉默了下来。迪纳兹阿德催促她姐姐如果能免于惩罚就继续讲下去。

paragraphs.en: On the eighty-first night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 在第八十一个夜晚，舍赫拉扎德说道：

paragraphs.en: Ja'far told the caliph that Badr al-Din Hasan sat next to a hunchback as his cousin entered. The attendants had prepared her meticulously: her hair was adorned with musk-scented braids, and she wore robes and jewelry fit for Persian kings.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔告诉哈里发，当那位堂亲进来时，巴德尔丁·哈桑正坐在一个驼背人的旁边。侍从们对她进行了精心打扮：她的辫子上点缀着散发麝香香气的珠饰，穿着足以媲美波斯国王的华贵长袍和珠宝。

paragraphs.en: The bride walked in, wearing a golden-embroidered robe with intricate designs of birds and beasts, their eyes and bills made of precious stones, feet of rubies and green beryl. Her face shone under the light of camphor candles, more radiant than the full moon on the fourteenth night. With her sharp eyes, long lashes, rosy cheeks, and graceful gait, she captivated everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 新娘穿着金线绣花的长袍，上面精细地绣着飞禽走兽，它们的眼睛和喙由珍贵宝石制成，脚则是红宝石和绿碧玺。在白千层烛光的照耀下，她的脸庞更加光彩夺目，胜过十四之夜满月的光辉。她那锐利的目光、长长的睫毛、粉嫩的双颊以及优雅的步伐，令所有人都为之倾倒。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Badr al-Din Hasan sat gracefully, drawing attention like the moon among stars. His brow was radiant, his neck as white as marble, his face bright as the moon, and his cheek bore a mole like ambergris.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，巴德尔·丁·哈桑优雅地坐着，犹如群星中的明月，引人注目。他的额头光采照人，脖子白皙如玉，脸庞皎洁似月，脸颊上的一颗痣仿佛凝脂般诱人。

paragraphs.en: As the bride approached, swaying gracefully, she unveiled her face. The hunchback attempted to kiss her but she turned away and stood before Badr al-Din Hasan, her cousin. This caused the singing women to cry out and the crowd to clamor.
paragraphs.zh: 新娘款步走来，身姿优雅地摇曳着，终于露出了面容。驼背试图吻她，但她却避开了，站在了堂兄弟巴德尔丁·哈桑面前。这一幕让歌女们惊呼起来，人群中也发出了一片喧闹声。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan, seeing his hand was full of dinars, began throwing them into the tambourines while the women commended him with their fingers, suggesting he wished for the bride as his own.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁·哈桑见自己手中握满了金币，便一边往鼓手的鼓中投掷，一边惹得众女指指点点，显然他心中早已将新娘纳入了自己的怀抱。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan smiled at the bride, surrounded by servants and slave-girls carrying trays of gold pieces. The servants scattered the coins among the guests. Meanwhile, the hunchback sat alone, like a monkey.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁·哈桑微笑着看着新娘，她被仆人和端着金块托盘的女奴们环绕。仆人们将金币散给了宾客。与此同时，驼背则独自坐在一旁，仿佛一只猴子。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad said to King Shahryar: "Ja'far told the caliph that they presented the bride in her first dress, swaying coquettishly, delighting everyone present, especially Badr al-Din Hasan. In her red satin dress, she was radiant like a sun above dunes, as praised by an excellent poet. They changed her into a blue dress, and she appeared like a shining moon with jet black hair, soft cheeks, and opulent limbs."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹尔对沙赫里亚尔王说：“贾法尔向哈里发禀报，他们将新娘穿着第一套婚纱展示出来，风情万种地摇曳着身姿，令在场的所有人都为之倾倒，尤其是巴德尔丁·哈桑。她身穿大红色的丝质长裙，犹如沙丘之上的太阳，正如一位杰出诗人的赞美之词。随后她们又换了一件蓝色的礼服，新娘仿佛一轮明月，乌黑的秀发、娇嫩的脸颊和丰盈的身体熠熠生辉。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri and Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri then dressed the woman in another gown. Her long black hair, as dark as night, veiled her face except for her eyes, which pierced hearts like arrows. The poet had said of such a beauty:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·埃及和巴德尔丁·哈桑·巴士拉随后给那女子换上另一件长袍。她长长的黑发如同夜色般漆黑，只露出眼睛，那双眼睛仿佛利箭一般穿透人心。诗人曾如此赞美这样的绝世佳人：

paragraphs.en: Veiling her cheeks with hair, she came to charm, And like a dove appeared to lovers' harm.
paragraphs.zh: 遮掩脸颊的秀发中，她款步而来，欲擒故纵；仿佛鸽羽般柔美的身姿，却让情人徒增伤感。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din remarked, "You veil the morning with the night." She replied, "No, I veil the moon from the light."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁脱口而出：“你用黑夜遮掩了清晨。”她回答说：“不，我是用月光遮住了光明。”

paragraphs.en: They dressed her in a fourth gown, and she emerged like the rising sun, swaying coquettishly. Her grace was like that of a deer, piercing hearts with her eyes. The poet had written:
paragraphs.zh: 他们给她穿上第四件长袍，她走出帷幕后如同初升的太阳，摇曳生姿。她的优雅犹如deer般灵动，眼神穿透人心。诗人写道：

paragraphs.en: The sun of beauty she to all appears, With coy reserve and with coquettish grace. And when the sun beholds her radiant smile, He in the clouds hastens to hide his face.
paragraphs.zh: 她对众人展现的是美丽之阳，带着羞涩的娇媚。当太阳见到她那灿烂的笑容时，便急忙躲到云后藏起了脸庞。

paragraphs.en: In the fifth gown, she revealed her wonders. She swayed her hips and shook her ringlets like a willow bough or a deer bending to drink. The poet described:
paragraphs.zh: 在第五段中，她展现了她的奇妙之处。她摇曳着腰肢，梳理着如柳枝般轻摆或似deer低首饮水的卷发。诗人如此描述：

paragraphs.en: She comes like a full moon on a fair night, With dainty limbs and with a slender waist. With eyes that subdue all men with their charm, With cheeks that vie with rubies at their best.
paragraphs.zh: 她如同良宵佳月下圆满的明月，身材修长，腰肢纤细。一双眼睛魅力无穷，令所有男人倾倒；双颊红润，胜过宝石中的珍品。

paragraphs.en: Her jet black hair trailed over her hips; beware the serpents of her curls, she warned. Her sides were soft, but a heart harder than stones lay hidden there. From arching brows, she sent darting looks, which never missed their mark.
paragraphs.zh: 她一头乌黑的长发垂至臀部；她警告说，要小心她那卷曲中的“毒蛇”。她的侧身柔软，但里面藏着一颗比石头还硬的心。从她高挑的眉宇间，射出的目光精准无比，从未落空。

paragraphs.en: In the sixth gown, green as emerald leaves, she reached the height of beauty. She shamed a bronze spear with her slender form and outshone the rising moon with her radiant face. The poet had said:
paragraphs.zh: 在第六段中，她身着翠绿的衣裙，美到了极点。她的身形纤细，令一支铜矛都显得黯然失色；她的容颜光艳照人，远胜初升的明月。诗人曾如此赞道：

paragraphs.en: There was a maid with such polish and grace That e'en the sun seemed borrowed from her face. Bedecked in green she came, fair to behold, As a pomegranate bud the green leaves enfold.
paragraphs.zh: 这位女仆举止优雅，风采动人，仿佛连太阳的光辉都是从她的脸庞借来的。她身着绿色衣裙翩然而至，美丽得如同绿叶环抱中的石榴花蕾。

paragraphs.en: When asked about this gown, she answered sweetly: "Since I have tortured many with my arts,..."
paragraphs.zh: 当被问及这件长袍时，她甜笑道：“因为我用我的技艺折磨过许多人……”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: "O King, Ja’far told the caliph that whenever the attendants presented the bride in a new dress and brought her before the hunchback, she would turn away from him and approach Badr al-Din Hasan. He would then give a handful of gold to the singing women. This continued until all seven dresses were unveiled.
paragraphs.zh: “国王陛下，贾法尔向哈里发禀报说，每当侍从们给新娘换上新装并把她带到驼背面前时，她总是避开他，走近巴德尔·丁·哈桑。于是，巴德尔·丁·哈桑便赏给歌女一把金币。这种情况一直持续到七件新装全部展示完毕。

paragraphs.en: The guests departed, leaving only Badr al-Din and the hunchback behind. As the attendants took the bride inside, the hunchback turned to Badr al-Din and said, 'You have cheered us with your presence. Please leave now.'
paragraphs.zh: 宾客散去，只剩下巴德尔丁和驼背留在原地。伴郎将新娘领入室内后，驼背转头对巴德尔丁说道：“你的到来让我们喜出望外，请你先行离开吧。”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din rose and went to the hallway where he was met by a demon and a she-demon. They instructed him to wait in the bedroom until the bride arrived, then pretend to be her husband and consummate their marriage. The hunchback had been hired for ten dirhams and a bowl of food, but they had no sympathy for him."
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁站起身，走向走廊，不料遇到了一个恶魔和一个雌妖。他们吩咐他在卧室里等待新娘的到来，然后假装是她的丈夫，并完成婚配。驼背雇来时只得到了十迪拉姆和一碗食物，但他们对他的遭遇却毫不怜悯。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued: "The king planned this all to laugh at the hunchback."
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德接着说：“国王策划这一切只是为了嘲笑那个驼背的人。”

paragraphs.en: The hunchback entered the privy and began defecating when a demon appeared as a black cat, saying "Meow." The cat grew into an ass-colt, braying loudly. Terrified, the hunchback smeared his legs with feces and cried for help.
paragraphs.zh: 驼背走进厕所，正要如厕时，一只黑猫突然出现，“喵”了一声。那猫瞬间化作一匹小驴驹，发出 loud 的叫声。驼背吓得腿上沾满了粪便，大声呼救。

paragraphs.en: The ass-colt then transformed into a buffalo, which spoke in a human voice: "Damn you, hunchback!"
paragraphs.zh: 这驴驹随即化作一头水牛，它用人的声音说道：“你这个驼背，咒死你！”

paragraphs.en: The hunchback was so frightened that he slipped on the toilet still dressed. The demon demanded, "You mean hunchback! Why did you marry my mistress?"
paragraphs.zh: 驼背吓得一屁股坐在了马桶上，衣服也没来得及脱。恶灵厉声问道：“你就是驼背！你怎么敢娶我的夫人？”

paragraphs.en: The hunchback replied, "I had no choice; they forced me to marry her and I didn't know she loved a buffalo." The demon threatened, "If you leave or speak before sunrise, I'll wring your neck. Depart now and never return."
paragraphs.zh: 驼背回答道：“我别无选择，他们逼迫我娶了她，而且我不知道她爱的是一头水牛。”恶魔威胁说：“如果你在日出前离开或说话，我会扭断你的脖子。你现在就走，永远不要回来。”

paragraphs.en: The demon then turned the hunchback upside down with his head in the toilet and feet up, warning him to stay until morning or face punishment.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，恶魔将驼背的人倒挂了起来，头在马桶里，脚朝上，警告他必须等到天亮，否则将受到惩罚。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan waited in the net as the hunchback entered the privy. The bride, Sit al-Husn, then came in, accompanied by an old woman who mocked the hunchback before leaving. Upon seeing Badr al-Din, Sit al-Husn expressed her desire to share him with the hunchback.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁·哈桑在网中等候，只见驼背进入了厕所。随后，Sit al-Hüsna新娘带着一位老妇人走了进来，那老妇人在嘲笑驼背后便离开了。见到巴德尔丁，Sit al-Hüsna表达了她愿意与驼背共享他的意愿。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din denied this, saying their marriage was a sham and that they had hired the hunchback for ten dirhams and food. Hearing his words, Sit al-Husn laughed and invited Badr al-Din to take her. He removed his trousers, placed the purse of thousand dinars inside them, and laid them under the mattress.
paragraphs.zh: 布达丁否认了这一点，说他们的婚姻只是个骗局，并且他们雇用了驼背，只给了十迪尔汗和一些食物。听到这话，希特胡森笑了，邀请布达丁娶她为妻。他脱下裤子，把装有一千第纳尔的皮囊放了进去，然后将它们放在了床垫下面。

paragraphs.en: After removing his turban, he stood hesitating until Sit al-Husn drew him closer, urging him to satisfy her desires. She recited verses expressing her longing for him.
paragraphs.zh: 摘下头巾后，他犹豫着站立不前，直到思·呼森拉近了身子，催促他满足她的渴望。她吟诵起表达自己对他深深思念的诗句。

paragraphs.en: Morning came before they could continue, and Shahrazad paused. Dinarzad commented on the story's entertainment value, prompting Shahrazad to promise an even better tale the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 天未亮他们便停了下来，沙赫拉兹阿德暂停了讲述。丁纳兹阿德对故事的趣味性发表了评论，沙赫拉兹阿德则承诺如果她能熬过今晚，明天晚上将带来一个更加精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began: Ja’far told the caliph...
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：“Ja’far向哈里发讲述……”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan and Sit al-Husn embraced. He took her virginity, and they lay down to sleep with their necks touching and cheeks pressed together.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁·哈桑和思特赫斯恩紧紧拥抱在一起。他破了她的处女之身，随后两人头挨着头、面颊紧贴地躺下休息。

paragraphs.en: Cleave to the one you love, ignore calumny, For those who envy never favor love.
paragraphs.zh: 依恋你所爱的人，ignore calumny意即不理会诽谤，For those who envy never favor love则可译为嫉妒者从不钟情。整句可以翻译为： 依恋你所爱的人，不理会诽谤；嫉妒者从不钟情。

paragraphs.en: Two lovers in one bed—no fairer sight Has mercy’s Lord created from above. Bosom to bosom in each other's arms, They lie in bliss, clad in their own delight.
paragraphs.zh: 一男一女共枕而眠——这世间何处寻觅更美的景象？ 慈悲的主创造了这般美景。他们相依偎，心贴着心，在彼此的怀抱中安睡，沉浸于各自的喜悦之中。

paragraphs.en: As they slept, the demon said to the she-demon: "Take up the young man and return him to where he was asleep before morning." The she-demon carried Badr al-Din Hasan, who lay naked except for a thin sequined shirt with Moroccan gold embroidery and his striped blue skullcap. They flew away as the angels shot them with shooting stars.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们熟睡时，妖魔对雌妖说：“把那个年轻人抱起来，天亮前送他回到原来睡觉的地方。”雌妖抱着巴德尔·丁·哈桑飞走了。只见他赤身裸体，仅穿着一件镶着闪亮sequin的薄纱长袍，上面绣有摩洛哥金色花纹，还戴着一顶蓝色条纹的头巾。此时，天使们向他们射来流星般的光芒。

paragraphs.en: The demon was consumed by fire, but the Almighty God saved the she-demon. She safely landed Badr al-Din Hasan at the city of Damascus just as fate would have it. There, she left him near one of the city gates and departed.
paragraphs.zh: 那恶魔被烈火吞噬，但至高无上的神明救下了雌魔。她安全地将巴德尔·丁·哈桑送到大马士革城中，仿佛命中注定一般。随后，她在城门外留下他，便离开了。

paragraphs.en: As dawn broke, the city gate opened. People emerged to find a young man, clad only in a light shirt and a skullcap, snoring deeply from the previous night's exertions. Some speculated, "What luck for him who spent the night with such a youth!
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，城门缓缓开启。人们走出家门，只见一位年轻人仅穿着一件轻便的衬衫和一顶小帽，正沉沉地打着鼾声。有人不禁猜测：“昨晚与如此英俊的年轻人共度一夜，真是他的幸运！”

paragraphs.en: He should have waited until he dressed properly." Another added, "How unfortunate for both of them! Look at this young man; perhaps he left a tavern drunk and fell asleep outside without clothes, or maybe he couldn't find his way home and ended up here."
paragraphs.zh: 他本该等穿好衣服再出来的。“真是不幸！”另一个人接着说，“看这个年轻人，或许他是喝醉了从酒馆出来，在外面没穿衣服就睡着了，或者可能是找不到回家的路，结果到了这里。”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri woke to the crowd's murmurs. Surprised by the commotion, he asked, "Good people, where am I? Why are you gathered around me?"
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁·哈桑·阿巴斯里醒来时，听见四周人群的低语声。他惊讶于这阵骚动，脱口问道：“各位大人，我在哪里？你们为什么都围在我身边？”

paragraphs.en: They replied, "We found you at the city gate during morning prayers. We know nothing else about your whereabouts last night." Badr al-Din responded, "By God, good people, I slept in Cairo last night."
paragraphs.zh: 他们回答说：“我们在晨祷时发现你正站在城门口。至于你昨晚的行踪，我们一无所知。”巴德尔·丁回应道：“天知道，好人们，我昨晚是在开罗睡觉的。”

paragraphs.en: One man said, "Listen to him!" Another suggested, "Kick him hard!" A third interjected, "Son, you must be mad; how can you sleep in one city and wake up in another?"
paragraphs.zh: 一个人喊道：“听他的！”另一个人建议说：“给他来一脚！”第三个插嘴道：“儿子，你一定是疯了；你怎么可能在一座城市睡觉，在另一座城市醒来呢？”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din recounted his journey: "Last night in Cairo, yesterday in Basra, and today in Damascus." His audience was divided. Some praised him, others called him mad.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁讲述了他旅途的经历：“昨晚在开罗，前天在巴士拉，今天又到了大马士革。”他的听众意见不一，有人称赞他，也有人认为他疯了。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din admitted he had been a bridegroom in Cairo that night but wondered if it was real or just a dream. He questioned where his belongings were if it was indeed a dream.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁承认那天晚上自己在开罗做过新郎，但他怀疑那是否是真实的经历还是仅仅是一场梦。他自问如果这确实是一场梦，自己的财物现在在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad marveled at the story, urging her sister to top it with an even better tale should the king spare them.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳札德被故事深深吸引，催促妹妹如果国王饶恕她们，一定要讲一个更加精彩的故事来超越这个。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: "Ja'far told the caliph of a king..."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉兹朵开始讲述：“贾法尔向哈里发说起一位国王……”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din Hasan fled when people called him mad. He entered a cook's shop where everyone retreated in fear. The cook, once a criminal but now reformed, adopted Badr as his son and provided him with new clothes.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁·哈桑一听到人们叫他疯子便仓皇而逃，最终躲进了一家小餐馆。店里的人都吓得退避三舍。这位厨师曾是罪犯，但现在已经改过自新了，收留了巴德尔，并为他购置了新的衣裳。

paragraphs.en: From then on, Badr was known as the cook’s son.
paragraphs.zh: 从那时起，巴德爾就被叫做厨子的儿子了。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Sit al-Husn woke up to find her cousin Badr missing. Thinking he had gone to relieve himself, she waited. Her father, Shams al-Din Muhammad, the Egyptian vizier, came to her room, upset about his forced marriage to a servant.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，思·赫森醒来发现表弟巴德不见了。她以为他去方便了，便耐心等待。她的父亲穆罕默德·沙姆斯丁·埃及首相——穆斯塔法·阿里·埃及首相前来房间，心情烦躁，因为他被迫娶了一个仆人做妻子。

paragraphs.en: He called out to his daughter, who emerged radiant and kissed him.
paragraphs.zh: 他朝女儿喊去，女儿光彩照人地走了出来，随即吻了他。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad paused, and Dinarzad remarked on the story's strangeness. Shahrazad hinted at an even more intriguing tale for the next night.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，沙赫拉兹停了下来，丁纳兹雅特对故事的怪异表示了评论。沙赫拉兹暗示接下来的夜晚将有一个更加引人入胜的故事。

paragraphs.en: When Sit al-Husn heard her father mock the hunchback, she defended herself. "Stop, father! I had a better night than ever before."
paragraphs.zh: 当思·呼森听到父亲嘲笑驼背时，她为自己辩解道：“住手，爸爸！这是我睡得最好的一夜。”

paragraphs.en: Her father glared and asked if the hunchback had slept with her. She replied, "I slept only with my true husband, who is handsome and has dark eyes."
paragraphs.zh: 她父亲怒目而视，问道：“那个驼背和你睡过吗？”她回答说：“我只和我的真夫睡过，他英俊且眼睛深邃。”

paragraphs.en: Her father went to the privy where he found the hunchback upside down in the toilet. He shouted at him, but the hunchback just said, "Yeah, yeah." The vizier asked why he was in that position, and the hunchback retorted, "Couldn't you find anyone for me except a girl who consorts with buffaloes?"
paragraphs.zh: 她的父亲走进厕所，只见驼背倒挂在马桶上。他大声喊道，但驼背只应了声：“嗯，嗯。” vizier 问道他为何要采取这种姿势，驼背反唇相讥：“难道你找不到比我更合适的人吗？我至少没和水牛鬼混过。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad commented, "Sister, what an entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德停下了讲述。丁纳札德说道：“姐姐，真是个精彩的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等明天晚上再听吧。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: Ja’far told the caliph a strange tale.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉兹朵开始讲述：贾法尔向哈里发讲述了一个奇怪的故事。

paragraphs.en: When the hunchback complained to the bride's father about marrying a girl who consorts with buffaloes and demons, the vizier ordered him out. The hunchback refused until dawn, recounting his encounter with a demon that turned into a buffalo. He then went to the king.
paragraphs.zh: 当驼背向新娘的父亲抱怨娶了一个与水牛和恶魔勾搭成奸的女子时，首相命令他滚蛋。驼背直到天亮都没离开，讲述了自己与一头变成水牛的恶魔相遇的经历。随后，他前往国王那里诉说此事。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the bride’s father confronted her, demanding she reveal her secret. She told him of a mysterious young man who had spent the night with her, taking her virginity and leaving behind his turban, robe, dagger, trousers, and a purse with a thousand dinars. The vizier examined the turban and found it belonged to Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，新娘的父亲质问她，要求她透露这个秘密。新娘告诉他，有一个神秘的年轻人在一夜之间与她共度，夺去了她的童贞，并留下了一顶土耳其帽、一件长袍、一把匕首、一条裤子以及一个装有一千第纳尔的荷包。 vizier 检查了那顶土耳其帽，发现它属于巴德尔丁·哈桑·阿巴斯里。

paragraphs.en: Inside was a sealed scroll containing evidence of a sale.
paragraphs.zh: 里面密封着一份卷轴，上面记载了某项交易的证据。

paragraphs.en: The vizier read the note: "Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri has sold to Isaac the Jew the cargo of the first ship for a thousand dinars." He fainted upon reading it.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 看完信件上的内容：“巴德尔·丁·哈桑·阿巴斯里把第一艘船的货物卖给了犹太人伊萨克，售价一千第纳尔。”他看完后竟然晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused, and Dinarzad exclaimed, “Sister, what an intriguing tale!” Shahrazad promised more the next night if she was spared.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德停顿了一下，迪纳尔扎德脱口而出：“姐姐，这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹阿德承诺如果她今晚能免于被处决，明天晚上还会讲更多。

paragraphs.en: The eighty-seventh night, Shahrazad began: Ja’far told the caliph...
paragraphs.zh: 第八十七夜，沙赫拉兹尔说道：贾法尔向哈里发讲述……

paragraphs.en: When Shams al-Din regained consciousness and realized what his brother Nur al-Din had done, he was stunned. Upon opening the sealed letter, which bore his brother’s handwriting, he exclaimed, "Daughter, do you know who took your virginity? It is none other than your cousin, and these thousand dinars are your dowry."
paragraphs.zh: 当沙姆斯·丁苏醒过来，意识到哥哥努尔·丁所做的一切后，他惊呆了。打开那封密封信件，看到上面写着哥哥的名字，他脱口而出：“女儿，你知道是谁夺走了你的童贞吗？正是你的堂兄，而这千第纳尔就是你的嫁妆。”

paragraphs.en: He then read the letter, noting the dates of Nur al-Din's arrival in Basra, their marriage contract, the birth of his son Badr al-Din-Hasan, and the year of his death. Shams al-Din was amazed to find that the events and dates mirrored his own life in Cairo. He concluded that Providence had orchestrated everything.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后读了这封信，注意到努尔·阿丁抵达巴格达的日期、他们的婚约、他的儿子_badr al-din hasan_出生的年份以及他去世的年份。沙姆斯·阿丁惊讶地发现，这些事件和日期竟然与他在开罗的生活如出一辙。他断定，这一切都是天意的安排。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din then took the letter and the paper from the purse, went directly to the king, and recounted the entire story. The king was equally astonished and ordered the events to be recorded.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁随后从皮囊中取出信件和纸张，径直走向国王，并将整个故事详细讲述了一遍。国王同样大为惊讶，当即下令将这些事件记录下来。

paragraphs.en: The vizier waited three days for his nephew but received no news. On the seventh day, frustrated, he decided to act. He wrote a detailed description of the wedding chamber and its contents, including the turban, trousers, and purse, then set them aside.
paragraphs.zh: 这位宰相等了侄子三天，却毫无音信。到了第七天，他已是焦躁不安，决定采取行动。他详细描述了婚房及其内物，包括头巾、裤子和钱袋，然后把这些东西放到了一边。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to tell you if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 随着黎明临近，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。丁纳兹阿德说道：“姐姐，这故事真是引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；如果国王饶恕我，我会给你讲更多。”

paragraphs.en: The eighty-eighth night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第八十八个夜晚，沙赫拉兹尔开始说道：

paragraphs.en: O happy King, Ja’far told the caliph that days and months passed. When the time came for the vizier's daughter of Egypt, she gave birth to a boy with a round face like the full moon or rising sun, a radiant brow, and rosy cheeks. They cut his umbilical cord and applied kohl to his eyelids.
paragraphs.zh: 幸福的国王啊，贾法尔对哈里发说，日子一天天过去，转眼间就到了埃及 vizier 的女儿分娩的日子。她生下一个圆脸如满月或朝阳般的孩子，眉宇间透着光彩，脸颊红润。他们剪断了脐带，并在孩子的睫毛上抹上了眼线膏。

paragraphs.en: His grandfather named him 'Ajib and entrusted him to the care of nurses, stewardesses, and servants.
paragraphs.zh: 他的祖父给他取名阿吉布，并将他托付给奶妈、女仆和仆人照料。

paragraphs.en: ’Ajib grew up and was sent to school at seven by his grandfather. He stayed there for four years before he began bullying other children. Eventually, they complained to the monitor about his behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉布长大后，七岁那年被祖父送进了学校。他在那里待了四年，之后开始欺负其他孩子。最终，那些孩子向班长投诉了他的行为。

paragraphs.en: The monitor suggested a plan: when ’Ajib arrived the next day, the children should gather around him and say that only those who knew their parents' names could join in their game.
paragraphs.zh: 监考官提议了一个方案：当阿吉布第二天到来时，孩子们应该围着他转，宣称只有知道父母姓名的人才能加入他们的游戏。

paragraphs.en: The following morning, the children gathered as instructed. One of them said, "We will play a game, but no one can join unless they tell us their mother's and father's names." They all agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，孩子们如约而至。其中一个孩子说：“我们来玩个游戏，但要想加入，必须先告诉我们你们父母的名字。”大家都欣然同意了。

paragraphs.en: Then each child introduced themselves, including Majid, Sittita, and ’Iz al-Din. When it was ’Ajib’s turn, he said his name and the names of his supposed parents: Sit al-Husn and Shams al-Din, the vizier.
paragraphs.zh: 然后每个孩子都作了自我介绍，包括玛吉德、西蒂塔和伊兹丁。轮到阿济布时，他脱口而出自己的名字和他的所谓父母的名字：希特·阿·胡森和沙姆斯·丁，那位首相。

paragraphs.en: The children laughed at him, saying, "How can that be? He is not your father!" ’Ajib insisted, but they continued to mock him.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子们嘲笑他，说：“怎么可能呢？他不是你的父亲！”阿吉布坚持自己的说法，但孩子们继续取笑他。

paragraphs.en: They told him that his grandfather was actually his maternal grandfather, and his real father was unknown since his mother had been married to a hunchback and impregnated by demons.
paragraphs.zh: 他们告诉他，他的祖父其实是他母亲的祖父，而他的生父至今不明，因为他的母亲曾嫁给一个驼背，并且被妖魔所孕。

paragraphs.en: The monitor then approached ’Ajib and explained the situation: even though Shams al-Din was his maternal grandfather, he did not know who his biological father was. The children would treat him as a bastard unless he found out his true parentage. He urged ’Ajib to understand that knowing one’s parents was important, especially when compared to his peers whose fathers were known.
paragraphs.zh: 监工随后走近阿吉布，解释了情况：虽然沙姆斯丁是他的外祖父，但他并不知道自己真正的生物学父亲是谁。如果不能查明身世，孩子们可能会把他当作私生子看待。他敦促阿吉布明白，了解自己的父母非常重要，尤其是在与那些父母亲人都为人所知的同学相比时更是如此。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: "O happy king, Ja'far told the caliph that when 'Ajib heard insults from children and a monitor, he ran home to his mother Sit al-Husn. She comforted him, asking who his father was. Sit al-Husn revealed that 'Ajib's father is the vizier of Egypt, not her own son.
paragraphs.zh: “可喜的国王啊，贾法尔告诉哈里发，当阿吉布听到孩子们和监工的侮辱时，他跑回家去找他的母亲思特·侯森。她安慰着他，问他父亲是谁。思特·侯森透露说，阿吉布的父亲是埃及的 vizier，并非她自己的儿子。

paragraphs.en: Overwhelmed with emotion, she recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 她情感激昂，脱口吟诵起这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: Love in my breast he lit and went away, Leaving an empty hearth and heart behind. His shrine too distant to visit now, A distance that keeps us worlds apart!
paragraphs.zh: 爱在他心中燃起，随后离去， 只留下空荡的家和孤寂的心。 如今他的圣殿遥不可及， 距离将我们隔得仿佛在两个世界！

paragraphs.en: When he left, so did my patience, endurance, self-control.
paragraphs.zh: 当他离开时，我的耐心、忍耐和自制力也随之耗尽。

paragraphs.en: He took all—my joy, peace, rest—and left me only tears of unhappy love, Falling from burning eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 他夺走了我所有的快乐、宁静和安宁，只留下无尽的悲伤之泪，从灼热的眼中滴落。

paragraphs.en: Longing to see him again, I trace his image in my heart, Welling with thoughts and deep passion.
paragraphs.zh: 渴望再次见到他，我心中不断勾勒他的身影，思绪万千，情意深浓。

paragraphs.en: Is there no ransom for the captive heart, No remedy for the afflicted, No medicine for the sick with love, No victory for the defeated?
paragraphs.zh: 俘获心灵的赎金何处寻？ 忧伤之人能否得慰藉？ 相思病患者又有何良药？ 败者何时能再赢？

paragraphs.en: O my dear love, how long this coy disdain? When will you return to be mine again?"
paragraphs.zh: 我亲爱的情人，你这矜持的冷漠要到何时？什么时候才能回到我的怀抱？

paragraphs.en: The vizier, Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri, entered his daughter's chambers to find her weeping with her son. Upon hearing their story about Badr al-Din Hasan’s disappearance, he joined them in tears. He then sought permission from the Egyptian king to travel eastward to Basra, requesting royal edicts for custody of his nephew wherever found.
paragraphs.zh: 埃及首相努尔·丁·阿里·米斯里走进女儿的房间，发现她正和儿子一起哭泣。听到他们讲述巴德·丁·哈桑失踪的故事后，他也忍不住流下了眼泪。随后，他向埃及国王请求准许前往东方的巴士拉，并恳请国王颁发诏书，以便在任何地方收养他的侄子。

paragraphs.en: The king granted his request and wrote letters and decrees. Overjoyed, the vizier thanked the king and returned home with his daughter and son 'Ajib, preparing for their journey.
paragraphs.zh: 国王答应了他的请求，书写了诏书和命令。喜出望外的 vizier 向国王道谢后，便带着女儿和儿子 ‘阿吉布 回家准备启程。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what a strange and engaging story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me; I have an even more captivating tale."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳兹德说道：“姐姐，这真是一个既奇异又引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等到明天晚上；我还有一篇更加扣人心弦的故事。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad recounted:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德说道：

paragraphs.en: Ja’far told the caliph that Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri, Badr al-Din’s uncle, traveled with his daughter and son 'Ajib for twenty days until they reached Damascus. There, they admired its rivers and birds, as described by a poet: "Once in Damascus I spent such a night / That time swore 't would never the like allow. / We slept carefree under the wing of night / Till morning smiled and beamed with dappled brow, / And dewdrops on the branches hung like pearls, / Then fell and scattered when the zephyr blew, / And birds chanted the words traced on the lake, / As the wind wrote and the clouds the points drew."
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔向哈里发禀报说，努尔丁·阿里·埃及的叔叔和他的女儿以及儿子阿吉布一起旅行了二十天，最终抵达大马士革。在那里，他们赞叹着诗人所描绘的河流和鸟儿：“曾在大马士革度过了那样一个夜晚 / 时间发誓再也不会让这样的时刻再现 / 我们在夜之羽翼下无忧无虑地酣眠 / 直到晨光微笑并以斑驳的脸庞示人 / 枝头挂着珍珠般的露珠 / 随着微风的吹拂而坠落散开 / 鸟儿歌唱着湖面上书写的诗句 / 仿佛是风在书写，云在勾勒笔画。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri and Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri rested at the Plain of Pebbles for a few days. Pages and servants went into Damascus to buy and sell, while ’Ajib explored the city with a eunuch carrying a red club made from knotted almondwood.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁·阿里·阿勒·密斯里和巴德尔·丁·哈桑·阿勒·巴斯里在鹅卵石平原歇息了几天。仆人们前往大马士革买卖，而阿吉布则带着一根红木制成的结节杏仁杖与一名太监一起探索城市。

paragraphs.en: In Damascus, people admired the young and beautiful ’Ajib, following him wherever he went. The eunuch stopped in front of Badr al-Din’s shop, where Badr al-Din had lived for twelve years after his adoptive father's death. Over time, Badr al-Din grew a beard and matured.
paragraphs.zh: 在大马士革，人们羡慕那位年轻而美丽的阿吉布，无论他走到哪里都备受追捧。太监停在巴德尔·丁的店铺前，这里他已经住了十二年，那是他亲生父亲去世后的事情了。随着时间流逝，巴德尔·丁长出了胡须，也逐渐成熟起来。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. The king resolved to find out what happened to the vizier and his family before executing her.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。国王决定在执行她的死刑之前查明那位 vizier 及其家人究竟发生了什么事。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued: I heard, O happy King, that Ja’far told the caliph:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德继续说道：幸福的国王啊，我听说贾法尔向哈里发禀告了：

paragraphs.en: When ’Ajib and his servant approached Badr al-Din’s shop, the father's heart raced as he admired his son’s beauty. He invited them in to taste his special pomegranate-seed dish cooked in sugar. Recalling his own days as a vizier’s son, tears welled up in his eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 当阿吉布和他的仆人走近巴德尔丁的店铺时，父亲的心跳加速，被儿子的英俊所吸引。他邀请他们品尝自己特制的糖煮石榴籽菜肴。回想起自己作为 vizier 儿子的日子，泪水不禁涌上眼眶。

paragraphs.en: “O my lord and master of my life and heart,” Badr al-Din said, “would you enter my shop? I would be happy to serve you.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我的主人和生命之主，”巴德尔丁说道，“您愿意光临我的店铺吗？我非常乐意为您服务。”

paragraphs.en: ’Ajib felt compassion for the cook and proposed entering the shop to console him. He hoped this act might reunite him with his father.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉布对厨师产生了同情之心，提议进去店里安慰他一番。他希望此举能让他与父亲重聚。

paragraphs.en: The eunuch, however, was angry. "What a fine thing for a vizier’s son to eat at a cookshop!" he said.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，那太监气愤地说：“宰相之子竟然在酒楼吃这种东西，真是岂有此理！”

paragraphs.en: “While I stand here protecting you from people's looks, how can I let you enter their shops?”
paragraphs.zh: “我在这里为你挡风遮雨，怎么能让你们进到那些店铺里去呢？”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din responded with verses: “I marvel that they guard you with one slave, While many are enslaved by your own grace.”
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁以诗回应：“我惊讶他们只用一个奴仆便将你守护，而许多人却在你的恩泽下沦为了奴隶。”

paragraphs.en: Turning to the eunuch, Badr al-Din added, "Noble lord, will you make me happy by entering my shop? You are like a chestnut, black without but white within."
paragraphs.zh: 转向太监，巴德尔·丁补充道：“高贵的老爷，您能否光临我的店铺让我高兴一番？您就像一颗栗子，外表黑而里面白。”

paragraphs.en: The eunuch laughed and asked, “For God’s sake, what did the poet say?” Badr al-Din recited: "Were he not such a fine and trusty man, He would not in the court hold such a sway, Or guard the harem with such zeal and care That even the angels do him homage pay."
paragraphs.zh: 太监笑道：“天哪，诗人说了些什么？”巴德尔·丁朗诵道：“若非此人贤能可靠，怎能在朝堂上拥有如此权势，又怎会如此尽心尽力地守护后宫，连天使都向他致敬。”

paragraphs.en: In darkness he excels, but it's his noble deeds that shine. This pleased the eunuch who laughed and took Ajib by the hand, entering Badr al-Din’s shop. A sizzling bowl of pomegranate seeds preserved with almonds and sugar was placed before them; they found it delicious.
paragraphs.zh: 在黑暗中他更显出色，但正是他的高尚行为让他更加耀眼。这令那太监十分满意，他笑着牵起阿吉布的手，一同走进巴德尔·丁的店铺。面前摆放着一碟用杏仁和糖腌制的石榴籽，味道鲜美，让他们赞不绝口。

paragraphs.en: Ajib turned to his father and said, "Sit down and eat with us, for I long to be reunited with my beloved." Badr al-Din replied, "Son, have you too suffered the loss of one you love?" Ajib wept, saying, "Yes, uncle; my heart aches for him.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉布转向父亲说道：“坐下和我们一起吃吧，我想念我的爱人了。”巴德尔丁回答道：“儿子，你也失去了所爱之人吗？”阿吉布流着泪说：“是的，叔叔；我的心在思念着他。”

paragraphs.en: My grandfather and I have searched far and wide in search of him."
paragraphs.zh: 我和祖父四处寻觅，希望能找到他。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din wept with his son, recalling his own separation from home and mother. He recited:
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁与儿子相拥而泣，回忆起自己离家别母的往事。他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: If ever we meet again, I will complain much to you. For no letter can heal the heart, Nor another voice a lover's pain.
paragraphs.zh: 如果将来再相见，我会向你诉说许多不满。因为任何信件都无法治愈心灵的伤痛，也无法缓解情人的痛苦。

paragraphs.en: The eunuch felt pity for Badr al-Din and took Ajib away after they ate together. But Badr al-Din could not bear their absence, closing his shop and following them.
paragraphs.zh: 太监怜悯巴德尔·丁，饭后将阿济带走了。但巴德尔·丁无法忍受他们的离去，关掉了自己的店铺，跟着他们走了。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "What is this compared to the tale I will tell you tomorrow night if I stay alive?"
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳札德说道：“姐姐，这真是个奇特又引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“比起我明天晚上还能活着讲述的故事来，这简直不算什么。”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din followed his son until they reached the Plain of Pebbles. Seeing him still behind, ’Ajib turned around, flushed with anger, and warned the eunuch to keep an eye on Badr al-Din. The eunuch instructed that if Badr al-Din turned in their direction upon exiting the city, they would know he was following.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁跟着儿子走，直到他们来到了鹅卵石平原。见儿子还落在后面，阿吉布转过身来，满脸怒气地对太监吩咐要留意巴德尔·丁的动向。太监指示说，如果巴德尔·丁在出城时朝他们这边看过来，他们就知道他在跟踪。

paragraphs.en: When Badr al-Din approached, ’Ajib became pale with fear of his grandfather's discovery and threw a stone at him, striking his forehead. Badr al-Din fainted, blood streaming down his face. The eunuch and ’Ajib hurried to their tents.
paragraphs.zh: 当巴德尔丁走近时，阿吉布害怕祖父发现他，吓得脸色苍白，朝他扔了一块石头，击中了巴德尔丁的额头。巴德尔丁顿时晕了过去，鲜血顺着他的脸流了下来。太监和阿吉布急忙赶回自己的帐篷。

paragraphs.en: Upon regaining consciousness, Badr al-Din bandaged his wound with his turban, blaming himself for following his son. He returned to his shop, where he occasionally missed his mother in Basra, wept, and recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: .Badr al-Din苏醒过来，用头巾包扎好伤口，自责跟着儿子走错了路。他回到了自己的店铺，在这里偶尔会怀念起在巴士拉的母亲，不禁落泪，并吟诵着这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began her tale to King Shahryar:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德向国王沙赫里亚尔讲述她的故事：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy king, that Ja’far told the caliph about two viziers. Badr al-Din returned to his shop and continued selling food. His uncle, the vizier, stayed in Damascus for three days before heading to Homs.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，贾法尔向哈里发讲述了两位宰相的故事。巴德尔·丁回到了他的店铺，继续卖食物。而他的叔叔——那位宰相，在大马士革逗留了三天后，前往霍姆斯。

paragraphs.en: After completing his search there, he moved on to Hama, spent a night, then pressed onward to Aleppo where he stayed for two days. He traveled through Dyarbakir, Mardin, Sinjar, and Mosul until reaching Basra.
paragraphs.zh: 完成在那里的搜寻后，他前往哈马度过了一夜，随后继续赶往阿勒颇，在那里住了两天。他又途经迪亚巴克尔、梅尔丁、辛贾尔和摩苏尔，最终抵达巴士拉。

paragraphs.en: Upon arriving, the vizier met with King Shahryar, who honored him and asked about his visit. Shams al-Din revealed that Nur al-Din Ali of Egypt was his brother, who had lived in the kingdom for fifteen years before dying, leaving behind a son who disappeared shortly after. The king’s old vizier's daughter, Nur al-Din’s mother, still resided there.
paragraphs.zh: 一到王宫，这位宰相便拜见了国王沙赫里yar。国王对他十分礼遇，并询问了他的来意。沙姆斯丁透露，埃及的努尔丁阿里是他的兄弟，曾在王国中居住了十五年，后去世，留下了一个儿子不久之后失踪了。而国王的老宰相的女儿、努尔丁的母亲至今仍住在那儿。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din requested permission to visit her and meet with her, which the king granted. He then went to his brother’s house, kissed the threshold, and remembered how Nur al-Din had died in a foreign land. Recalling this, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁请求国王允许他去探望她并会面，国王应允了。随后，他前往哥哥家中，在门槛上吻了一下，不禁想起了努尔丁死在异国的情景。想到这里，他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: I walk through halls where Leyla once lived, And weep upon the stone walls in my grief. ’Tis not for the stones that I yearn with love, But for the dear one who dwelt within those walls.
paragraphs.zh: 我漫步在莱拉曾经居住的走廊之中， 在悲痛中泪水滴落在石墙上。 我不是为了石头而倾注深情， 而是怀念那些墙壁之内所居住的爱人。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering the main gate, he found himself in a spacious courtyard with an arched door adorned with granite and multicolored marble. Walking around the house, he noticed his brother Nur al-Din’s name inscribed in gold and lapis lazuli on the walls. Kissing the inscription, he wept for his lost brother and recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 踏入大门，他发现自己置身于一个宽敞的庭院之中，庭院里有一扇拱门，门上镶嵌着花岗岩和多种彩色大理石。他在房子里转了一圈，注意到哥哥努尔·阿尔丁的名字用金色和青金石在墙上镌刻着。他亲吻着这些文字，为失去的兄弟而泪流满面，并吟诵起这几行诗句：

paragraphs.en: I ask for news of you the rising sun And of the lightning's flash of you inquire In passion's throes pass my night, Without complaining of love’s hellish fire. O my love, if our parting longer lasts My pining heart with pain will waste away But if you bless my sad eyes with your sight The day we meet will be a blessed day.
paragraphs.zh: 我向初升的太阳询问你的消息 也祈求闪电般迅疾的消息 在情欲的煎熬中度过漫漫长夜， 未曾抱怨爱火带来的痛苦。 哦，我的爱人，若我们的分别久长 我憔悴的心将因思念而枯萎 但如果你怜悯地出现在我眼前 我们重逢的日子必将是幸福的时光

paragraphs.en: Think not that I have found another love; There is no room for others in my heart. Pity a tortured lover, sick with love, Whose heart by parting has been torn apart. If fate should bless my sad eyes with your sight, I would that day offer my thanks to fate.
paragraphs.zh: 不要以为我找到了另一份真爱；我的心已无余地容纳他人。可怜这颗因离别而痛苦、病入膏肓的心吧。如果命运让我悲伤的眼眸再次见到你，那一天我会把感激献给命运。

paragraphs.en: May God defeat all those who wish us ill And thwart those who slander to separate.
paragraphs.zh: 但愿上帝击败所有对我们怀有恶意的人，并挫败那些造谣生事、离间我们关系的恶徒。

paragraphs.en: He then entered the hall and stopped at its door. The widow of his brother, Badr al-Din Hasan of Basra, had wept daily for years after her son’s disappearance. She continued to mourn by draping herself in flowing hair over a tomb she had built in the middle of the hall.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后走进大厅，在门口停了下来。他的弟弟巴德尔丁·哈桑·巴士里寡妇每天都在为儿子的失踪而哭泣，一连好几年都是如此。她继续哀悼，披着长发坐在大厅中央为自己建造的墓前。

paragraphs.en: Hearing her weeping and reciting these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 听到她的哭泣声和吟诵这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: O tomb, O tomb, has he his beauties lost, Or have you lost yourself that radiant look? O tomb, neither a garden nor a star, The sun and moon at once how can you host?
paragraphs.zh: 哦古墓，哦古墓，他的光彩是否消逝？还是你那光辉的容颜已不再？哦古墓，既非花园亦非星辰，如何同时容纳太阳与明月？

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad’s brother-in-law informed the widow that he was her brother-in-law and told her what had happened. But morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 沙哈拉兹德的妹夫向寡妇说明了他是她的妹夫，并告诉她发生了什么。但天色渐亮，沙哈拉兹德却沉默不语。

paragraphs.en: Dinarzad then said, "What a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "This is nothing compared to what I will tell you tomorrow night if I am alive."
paragraphs.zh: 迪纳兹达then说道：“这真是个奇特而有趣的故事！”沙赫拉扎德回答说：“比起我明天晚上要告诉你的故事，这简直不算什么。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Ja’far said to the caliph:
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，贾法尔对哈里发说道：

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din informed her about Badr al-Din's visit ten years ago. He had spent a night at their house but disappeared in the morning after spending time with Shams al-Din’s daughter, who became pregnant. The child born was Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁告诉她，十年前巴德尔丁曾来访。他在他们家过了一夜，随后与沙姆斯丁的女儿共度时光，后者因此怀孕。他们的孩子名叫努尔丁·阿里·埃及。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din’s mother learned of her son’s survival and rushed to see her brother-in-law. She fell at his feet, wept, and recited verses expressing joy at the news.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁的母亲得知儿子幸存的消息后，急忙赶到哥哥那里。她跪倒在哥哥面前，泪流满面，并诵读了几行表达喜悦之情的诗句。

paragraphs.en: She then embraced Ajib, kissed him, and wept. The vizier urged her not to grieve but to prepare for a journey to Egypt with them, hoping they might find Badr al-Din. He also suggested writing down this story.
paragraphs.zh: 她随即拥抱着阿吉布，吻了他，并流下了眼泪。那宰相劝慰她说不要悲伤，而是准备和他们一起前往埃及的旅程，希望能在那里找到巴德尔·丁。他还建议把这段故事记录下来。

paragraphs.en: The vizier left to bid farewell to the king, who provided gifts for their journey to Egypt.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 离开去向国王告别，国王赠予他一些礼物，以备他们前往埃及的旅途之需。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din left Basra on his way home and stayed in Aleppo for three days before continuing to Damascus. He pitched his tents near the city and planned to stay two or three days to buy fabrics and gifts for the king.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁离开巴士拉回家，在艾尔萨利停留了三天，之后继续前往大马士革。他在城外扎营，并计划在那里逗留两三天，为国王购买布料和礼物。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, 'Ajib suggested they visit the city. They walked through the Heavenly Gate into Damascus and spent time at the Umayyad Mosque until close to afternoon prayer. Then they entered the Grand Market and found Badr al-Din Hasan's shop.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，阿吉布建议他们去逛逛这座城市。两人穿过天门进入了大马士革，并在乌mayyad清真寺逗留了一段时间，直到接近傍晚的祈祷时间。随后，他们走进了大市场，找到了巴德尔·丁·哈桑的店铺。

paragraphs.en: He was preparing a pomegranate-seed dish, rich in almonds and sweet julep, flavored with cardamom and rosewater.
paragraphs.zh: 他正在准备一道石榴籽菜肴，富含杏仁和甜薄荷酒，调味用的是小豆蔻和玫瑰水。

paragraphs.en: When 'Ajib saw the dark scar on his father’s face from their previous encounter, he felt compassion. "Peace be with you!" he said.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉布看到父亲脸上上次相遇留下的深疤，心中涌起怜悯之情。“愿安拉保佑你！”他脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din's heart fluttered as he looked at his son, struggling to speak but eventually raising his head and reciting:
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁看着儿子，心里一阵紧张，尽管儿子努力想要开口，最终还是抬起头来诵读道：

paragraphs.en: "I longed to see the one I love, And when I did, I stood before him dumb and blind. I bowed my head in reverence and awe, But failed to hide the love that seethed behind."
paragraphs.zh: 我渴望见到我所爱的人，当我如愿以偿地站在他面前时，却变得哑口无言、目瞪口呆。我低头表示敬意与敬畏，但内心的情感依然无法掩饰。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din then invited 'Ajib and Shams al-Din to his shop for food. "Perhaps you will enter my shop," he said, "and eat my food to heal my broken heart. I cannot look at you without a throbbing in my heart."
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁随后邀请阿吉布和沙姆斯丁到他的店铺用餐。“或许你们可以进来我的店铺，”他说，“品尝一下我的食物，以此治愈我破碎的心。每次见到你们，我的心都会隐隐作痛。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: "O happy king, Ja'far told me that when Badr al-Din followed his sons, he was beside himself with worry. 'Ajib replied, 'You must be very fond of us. You gave us a mouthful of food and tried to dishonor us by assuming we owed you something.
paragraphs.zh: “可喜的君王，贾法尔告诉我，当巴德尔·丁跟随他的儿子们时，他忧心如焚。阿吉布回应道：‘你一定非常喜爱我们吧。你给了我们一口饭吃，并试图玷污我们的名声，以为我们会欠你什么。’”

paragraphs.en: This time, unless you swear not to follow or make any claims on us, we won't visit again.' They stayed for about a week so Badr al-Din's grandfather could buy presents for the king of Egypt."
paragraphs.zh: 这次，除非你保证不再跟踪我们或提出任何要求，否则我们将不会再来了。”他们住了大约一个星期，以便巴德尔·丁的祖父能为埃及国王购买礼物。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din agreed, ladling food and placing it before his son. 'Ajib said, "Sit down and eat with us," and Badr al-Din happily joined them, staring at his son. 'Ajib laughed, saying, "Ha, ha, haven't I told you that you are an overbearing lover?
paragraphs.zh: Badr al-Din同意了，他盛了一碗食物放在儿子面前。‘阿吉布说：“坐下来和我们一起吃吧。”Badr al-Din高兴地加入了他们，目光紧紧盯着自己的儿子。‘阿吉布笑道：“哈哈，我不是已经告诉过你，你是个专横的恋人吗？”

paragraphs.en: Stop staring at my face!"
paragraphs.zh: 住嘴盯着我的脸看！

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din sighed and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁叹了口气，吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: Passion for you lies deeply in the heart, A secret sealed in darkness, seen by none. O you whose beauty shames the shining moon, Whose ample grace rivals the rising sun, Your radiant face frustrates the burning heart And with hopelessness afflicts love's desire.
paragraphs.zh: 对你的情愫深深埋藏在心底，如同隐秘的誓言，无人知晓。你那胜过明月的美貌，与初升太阳般的风姿相媲美。你的容光焕发令人心旌摇动，绝望却让爱意更加炽热。

paragraphs.en: Your mouth is nectar, but I die of thirst; Your face is Heaven, but I burn in fire.
paragraphs.zh: 你的嘴如甘露，但我渴死；你的脸似天堂，但我却在火中煎熬。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din served ’Ajib and the eunuch until they were satisfied. He then washed their hands with water, offered them a towel, and sprinkled rosewater on them. Running out of the shop, he returned with a sweet drink cooled with snow and invited them to complete his kindness by drinking it.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁侍奉阿吉布和太监直到他们满意为止。随后，他用清水为他们洗手，递上毛巾，并在他们手上洒了些玫瑰水。跑出店铺后，他又返回来端了一杯冰镇的甜饮，请他们喝完这杯饮料以完成他的好意。

paragraphs.en: They passed the pitcher around until full, then thanked Badr al-Din and hurried back to their tents.
paragraphs.zh: 他们轮流传递水罐，直到装满后，便向巴德尔丁表示感谢，然后匆匆返回各自的帐篷。

paragraphs.en: ’Ajib visited his grandmother, who kissed him and wept, thinking of her son. She recited verses expressing her love for him despite their separation. ’Ajib ate a pomegranate-seed dish with bread, while the eunuch barely touched it.
paragraphs.zh: 阿吉拜去看望祖母，祖母亲吻了他，想起自己的儿子不禁落泪。她吟诵了几句表达对他的爱意的诗句，尽管他们已经分离。阿吉拜吃着石榴籽拌面包，而太监则几乎连碰都没有碰。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked on the story’s strangeness, to which Shahrazad replied that tomorrow's tale would be even more captivating if she survived another night.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳兹德对这个故事感到有些诧异，沙赫拉兹德则回应说，如果她能再熬过一夜的话，明天的故事将会更加引人入胜。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began: Ja’far told the caliph a story.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉泽达开始讲述：贾法尔向哈里发讲了一个故事。

paragraphs.en: The eunuch sat down, his belly already full. ’Ajib dipped bread in pomegranate juice but found it tasteless. "Bah," he said, "what is this awful stuff?"
paragraphs.zh: 太监坐了下来，肚子已经胀满。阿吉布把面包蘸在石榴汁里，却发现味道不佳。“唉，”他叹了口气，“这东西真难吃。”

paragraphs.en: His grandmother was shocked and accused him of criticizing her cooking. ’Ajib replied that they had tasted a better dish in the city. Angered, his grandmother confronted the eunuch, who denied eating anything.
paragraphs.zh: 他的祖母大为震惊，指责他批评她的烹饪。阿吉布则回答说，他们在城里尝过更美味的食物。祖母一听气得不行，立刻质问太监，而太监坚称自己什么也没吃。

paragraphs.en: However, ’Ajib insisted they had eaten at a cookshop.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，阿吉布坚持说他们是在一家小餐馆吃的。

paragraphs.en: The vizier, Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri, became angry and demanded to know where the eunuch had taken his grandson. The eunuch continued to deny it until the vizier challenged him with a bowl of pomegranate seeds. Taking a morsel, the eunuch could not swallow another and spat out what he had eaten, declaring that he was already full from the previous day's meal.
paragraphs.zh: 埃及首相努尔·丁·阿里·阿勒·密斯里气愤不已，质问太监究竟把他的孙子带到哪里去了。太监一再否认，直到首相用一碗石榴籽来逼问他。太监拈起一颗石榴籽，刚入口便再也咽不下去，只好吐了出来，声称自己已经饱了，昨天的饭量足够应付今天。

paragraphs.en: By this, Badr al-Din's vizier realized the truth. He ordered his servants to punish the eunuch, who cried for mercy, claiming they had eaten a better pomegranate dish at a cookshop. This angered Badr al-Din’s mother, who demanded he fetch her a bowl of the same dish from the cook.
paragraphs.zh: 就这样，巴德尔丁的首相明白了真相。他命令仆人惩罚那太监，而太监哭着求饶，声称他们在一家酒馆吃到了更美味的石榴羹。这激怒了巴德尔丁的母亲，她要求巴德尔丁亲自去给她端一碗同样的羹来。

paragraphs.en: The eunuch agreed and went to the cookshop, where Badr al-Din laughed and said only he and his mother could make such a dish. He prepared it and gave it to the eunuch, who returned with it. Upon tasting, Badr al-Din’s mother recognized her son's handiwork and fainted.
paragraphs.zh: 宦官同意了，便去了饭馆。巴德尔·丁·哈桑笑着对他说，只有他和他母亲才能做出这样的佳肴。他精心准备好了这道菜，并交给了宦官。宦官带回了菜肴，巴德尔·丁的母亲尝了一口后，立刻认出了儿子的手艺，当场晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night to hear more if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 天色渐亮，沙赫拉兹默不作声。迪纳兹达说道：“姐姐，这个故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹达回答道：“只有等到明天晚上国王饶恕我后才能听更多。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: O King, Ja’far told the caliph:
paragraphs.zh: 国王啊，贾法尔向哈里发禀告道：

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din's mother boasted that only her son could cook the dish perfectly. Upon hearing this, the vizier felt a mix of joy and sorrow, vowing to reunite with his nephew. He gathered fifty followers, instructing them to break into the cookshop and bring Badr al-Din bound but unharmed.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁的母亲夸耀说，只有她的儿子才能把这道菜做得完美无缺。听到这话， vizier 内心交织着喜悦与哀伤，暗下决心要与侄子团聚。他召集了五十名随从，吩咐他们破门而入，将巴德尔·丁绑起来但不要伤害他。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the vizier rode to the palace and met with the viceroy of Damascus. Showing him the king's edicts, the viceroy asked who their adversary was. The vizier replied that it was a cook.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，宰相骑马前往宫殿，与大马士革的总督会面。他向总督出示了国王的诏书，并询问对方的对手是谁。宰相回答说，对手是一名厨师。

paragraphs.en: The viceroy then sent a chamberlain with four captains, four guards, and six soldiers to the cookshop.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，总督派了一名内务大臣，带领四名队长、四名护卫和六名士兵前往饭馆。

paragraphs.en: Upon arrival, they found the shop in ruins, everything broken.
paragraphs.zh: 一进门，他们发现店铺一片狼藉，所有东西都被砸得粉碎。

paragraphs.en: While Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri was at the palace, his servants rushed out with sticks and swords. They stormed into Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri's cookshop without warning. They broke pots, utensils, shelves, bowls, dishes, and stoves.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁·阿里·埃及在宫中时，他的仆人们手持棍棒刀剑匆匆而出。他们毫无预警地冲进了巴德尔丁·哈桑·巴士里的小餐馆，肆意破坏，摔碎了锅碗瓢盆、架柜和炉灶。

paragraphs.en: When Badr al-Din asked, "What is wrong?" they accused him of cooking the pomegranate dish that the eunuch had bought. He defended himself but was still abused and dragged out of his shop by a crowd.
paragraphs.zh: 当巴德尔丁问道：“怎么了？”他们指控他烹饪了太监买来的石榴菜肴。尽管他极力为自己辩护，但仍遭到了辱骂，并被一群人大声喊叫着拖出了店铺。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night to hear more if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德停下了讲述。迪纳兹达说道：“姐姐，这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“只有国王不杀我，才能在明晚听更多。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: O King, Ja’far told the caliph:
paragraphs.zh: 国王啊，贾法尔向哈里发禀告道：

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din cried out, asking what was wrong with the pomegranate dish he had prepared. The chamberlain and his men caught up, hitting Badr al-Din and dragging him to the tents. Upon arrival, they waited for the vizier Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri to return.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁脱口而出，询问他精心准备的石榴果盘出了什么问题。宦官和他的随从赶了上来，打了巴德尔丁一顿，并把他拖到了帐篷里。到达后，他们等待着另一位 vizier 纳尔丁·阿里·埃及王子努尔·阿尔丁·阿利·米斯里 返回。

paragraphs.en: As soon as Nur al-Din dismounted, he asked where the cook was. They brought Badr al-Din before him. Seeing his uncle Shams al-Din, Badr al-Din wept and pleaded, "My lord, what have I done?"
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁一落地，便问厨子在哪里。仆人们领着巴德·丁来到他面前。见到叔叔沙姆斯·丁，巴德·丁不禁泪流满面，哀求道：“大人，我究竟做错了什么？”

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din replied harshly, "You cooked the pomegranate dish!" Badr al-Din cried out in frustration, asking if such a crime deserved death. Shams al-Din said it was only the beginning of punishment.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁冷硬地回应道：“你把石榴炖得一塌糊涂！”巴德丁沮丧地喊道，问这样的罪行是否该判死刑。沙姆斯丁说这只是惩罚的开始。

paragraphs.en: Shams al-Din ordered his servants to pack up and leave. They quickly dismantled the tents and loaded the camels. Badr al-Din was placed in a chest, locked, and carried away.
paragraphs.zh: 沙姆斯丁命令仆人们收拾行装离开。仆人们迅速拆卸了帐篷，并将骆驼装载完毕。巴德尔丁被放入一个箱子里，锁好后被人带走。

paragraphs.en: The group journeyed until nightfall, when they stopped for food. After feeding him, they locked him back up and continued their journey.
paragraphs.zh: 一行人赶路直到天黑，便停了下来用餐。喂饱他之后，他们把他重新关了起来，继续前行。

paragraphs.en: They continued their journey until they reached Cairo. Upon arrival, the vizier ordered Badr al-Din to be brought out of the chest and presented to him. The vizier instructed a carpenter to make a cross-like figure.
paragraphs.zh: 他们继续前行，最终抵达开罗。一到城中，首相便下令将巴德尔·丁从匣子里带出来，呈现在自己面前。他还吩咐木匠制作了一个十字架形状的图案。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din asked, "What will you do with it?" The vizier replied, "I will crucify you for the pomegranate dish lacking pepper and tasting awful."
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁问道：“你打算怎么处置我？”那首相答道：“我要把你钉在十字架上，为的就是这没有胡椒、味道糟糕的石榴羹。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad was interrupted by dawn, but Dinarzad encouraged her: "What an intriguing story!" Shahrazad responded, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me!"
paragraphs.zh: 拂晓打断了沙赫拉兹德，但丁扎兹德鼓励她说：“多引人入胜的故事啊！”沙赫拉兹德回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等到明天晚上吧！”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: Ja'far told the caliph that Badr al-Din said, "You have beaten and ruined my shop because of the pomegranate dish lacking pepper. Isn't it enough to tie me in a chest day and night, feed me only one meal, and torture me? Why must I be crucified for this?"
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔对哈里发说，巴德尔·丁说道：“你因为我那缺少胡椒的石榴菜而打砸了我的店铺，这已经够了！难道把我关在箱子里日夜不放，只给我一顿饭吃，折磨我就不够吗？为什么还要处以磔刑？”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din was bewildered and asked, "What should my punishment be if I did cook without pepper?" The vizier replied, "Crucifixion." Badr al-Din lamented, "Alas, will you crucify me because of the pomegranate dish lacking pepper?"
paragraphs.zh: _badr al-din 感到困惑，问道：“如果我真的没放胡椒粉就烹饪了那道菜，我应该受什么样的惩罚？” vizier 回答说：“处以十字架刑。” badr al-din 唶道：“唉，难道因为我做的石榴Soup 缺少胡椒粉就要处以十字架刑吗？”

paragraphs.en: He wept and declared, "No one has suffered as much as I have. May God curse the pomegranate dish!"
paragraphs.zh: 他泪流满面，脱口而出：“我受的苦无人能及。但愿苍天诅咒这石榴羹！”

paragraphs.en: When they brought the nails, Nur al-Din cried and mourned his impending crucifixion. As night fell, the vizier locked Badr al-Din in a chest, saying he would be nailed tomorrow. Badr al-Din sat inside, praying and lamenting his fate.
paragraphs.zh: 当钉子被拿来时， Nur al-Din 呜咽着哀悼自己即将面临的 crucifixion。夜幕降临，首相将 Badr al-Din 锁进一个箱子里，说他明天才会被钉上钉子。Badr al-Din 被困在箱子里，一边祈祷一边为自己的命运哀叹。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the vizier placed the chest on a camel and brought it to his house after the markets closed. He instructed his daughter Sit al-Husn to prepare the house as it was on their wedding night twelve years ago. The servants arranged everything exactly as he described, lighting candles and placing Badr al-Din's belongings in their original spots.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时， vizier 将箱子放在骆驼上，市场一打烊便将其带回家中。他吩咐女儿 Sit al-Husn 把家布置得如同十二年前他们举行婚礼的夜晚一样。仆人们按照他的描述一一安排妥当，点燃了蜡烛，并将 Badr al-Din 的物品放回原位。

paragraphs.en: The vizier then told his daughter to undress and go to bed, repeating what she should say if her husband came. She was to tell him he had stayed too long in the privy, engage him in conversation until morning, when they would reveal the whole story.
paragraphs.zh: 于是， vizier 让女儿脱衣上床，并告诉她如果丈夫回来时该说的话。她要告诉丈夫他在厕所待得太久，然后与他交谈直到天亮，到时候再把整个故事都说出来。

paragraphs.en: But Shahrazad did not continue the tale that night. Instead, Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "This is nothing compared to what I will tell you tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 但是莎赫拉兹德当晚并未继续这个故事。取而代之的是，丁达尔兹说道：“姐姐，这真是个奇怪而又引人入胜的故事！”莎赫拉兹德回答道：“比起我明天晚上要告诉你的故事来，这简直不算什么。只有国王饶恕了我，你才能听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: Ja'far told the caliph that he heard the vizier visit Badr al-Din. He untied him, stripped him of his clothes except for a shirt, and led him slowly to the room where the bride had been unveiled and where they had spent their night together.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔向哈里发禀报，说他听到那位 vizier 去拜访了巴德尔丁。他松开了巴德尔丁的束缚，只给他留下一件衬衫，然后慢慢把他带到了新娘曾被揭开面纱的地方，也是他们共度良宵之处的房间。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din entered the room, recognizing it instantly. The bed, net, and chair brought back memories from ten years ago, leaving him bewildered. He rubbed his eyes, muttering, "Glory be to God!
paragraphs.zh: Badr al-Din 进入房间，瞬间认出了这个地方。那张床、网和椅子勾起了他十年前的回忆，让他感到困惑不已。他揉了揉眼睛，喃喃自语道：“谢天谢地！”

paragraphs.en: Am I awake or asleep?"
paragraphs.zh: 我这是在做梦吗？还是已经醒来？

paragraphs.en: Sit al-Husn lifted the net and invited Badr al-Din inside, saying he had been away too long in the privy. Upon seeing her face, he smiled and agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 席·阿斯恩提起网子，邀请巴德尔·丁进来，说他在厕所待得太久了。只见她那张脸，他不禁微笑，欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: As he entered, memories flooded back, causing him confusion. He examined the turban, robe, and dagger on the chair, then felt under the mattress for his trousers and purse. Finally, he burst into laughter, exclaiming, "By God, this is a good one!"
paragraphs.zh: 他一进门，往事便如潮水般涌上心头，让他感到困惑。他仔细查看了椅子上的头巾、长袍和匕首，然后在床垫下摸索着寻找裤子和钱包。最后，他突然大笑起来，脱口而出：“天哪，这真是个好主意！”

paragraphs.en: Sit al-Husn asked why he was staring at the room and laughing. Badr al-Din laughed again and inquired how long he had been away from her.
paragraphs.zh: Sit al-Husn问.Bad尔·丁为何盯着房间笑个不停。Bad尔·丁再次笑了起来，然后询问自己离开她有多久了。
