paragraphs.en: She replied that he had only gone to relieve himself moments ago, asking if he had lost his wits.
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说刚才他还只是去方便了一下，质疑他是不是神智不清了。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din laughed. "By God, lady, you are right. I left you and fell asleep in the privy, dreaming of working as a cook in Damascus for ten years.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔丁笑道：“天哪，夫人，您说的没错。我离开您后，在厕所里睡着了，梦到在大马士革做了十年厨师。”

paragraphs.en: A young boy hit me with a stone, cutting my forehead. Then, I dreamt of going to Damascus without turban or trousers, cooking a pomegranate dish missing pepper. If I hadn't woken up, they would have crucified me."
paragraphs.zh: 一个少年用石头砸中了我的额头。随后，我梦见自己赤身裸体地去了大马士革，还煮了一道缺少胡椒的石榴菜肴，若不醒来，他们可能会把我钉在十字架上。

paragraphs.en: Sit al-Husn asked, "What else did you dream?" Badr al-Din replied, "They smashed my dishes, ruined my shop, tied and shackled me in a chest. A carpenter made a wooden cross to nail me on—due to the missing pepper."
paragraphs.zh: Sit al-Husn问道：“你还梦到了什么？”Badr al-Din回答说：“他们摔碎了我的瓷器，捣毁了我的店铺，把我锁在了一个箱子里。一个木匠还给我做了一根木十字架，打算钉死我——因为缺少了胡椒。”

paragraphs.en: He added, "Thank God it was all just a dream."
paragraphs.zh: 他叹了口气，说道：“谢天谢地，原来只是个梦。”

paragraphs.en: Sit al-Husn laughed, hugging him close. But Badr al-Din reflected again: "By God, my lady, what happened must have been real, but there is no power save in God. What a strange story!"
paragraphs.zh: Sit al-Husn 笑着将他紧紧拥入怀中。但布达丁再次沉思道：“天哪，夫人，这件事必定是真实的，然而除了上帝，我们无力改变什么。真是个奇异的故事！”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德沉默下来。丁纳兹阿德说：“姐姐，这真是个奇怪又引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答道：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等明天晚上吧。”

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din lay confused, switching between dreams and reality as he looked around the room at the bride. He muttered, "I have not even spent a night with her." His uncle entered, greeting him in the morning.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁困惑不已，梦境与现实交织在一起。他环视着房间，目光落在新娘身上。喃喃自语道：“连一个夜晚都没有陪过她。”这时他的叔叔走了进来，在晨光中向他问好。

paragraphs.en: Badr al-Din recognized his uncle but was bewildered when reminded of the beating and torture ordered for the pomegranate dish incident. The vizier explained that he had only wanted to confirm the marriage consummation by recognizing his belongings—turban, clothes, gold purse, and a scroll hidden in the turban lining.
paragraphs.zh: 巴德尔·丁认出了他的叔叔，但当提到石榴料理事件中下令的鞭打和折磨时，他还是感到困惑。 vizier 解释说，他只是为了确认婚事是否 consummated ，才认领了自己的财物——头巾、衣物、金囊以及藏在头巾里的卷轴。

paragraphs.en: The vizier then recited: "Our fate is fickle, for such is our state, That one day may depress, one day elate."
paragraphs.zh: 于是 vizier 唱道：“命运多舛，恰如我们的境况，或使一日忧郁，或令一日欢畅。”

paragraphs.en: He called Badr al-Din's mother, who embraced him with tears. She read her verses: "When we meet, we will complain Of our afflictions, that day, For the feelings of the heart No messenger can convey, Nor is the voicing of grief Keeping the feelings at bay. No messenger ever knows How to say what I can say."
paragraphs.zh: 他喊道，_badr al-din的母亲泪眼婆娑地扑过来拥抱了他。她念起了自己的诗句：“相逢时我们只会倾诉/那些痛苦的遭遇；/心灵的感受啊，/连信使也无法传达，/而哭泣也难以排遣心中的忧伤。/没有哪个信使能说出我此刻想说的话。”_

paragraphs.en: They shared their suffering and thanked God for their reunion. The next day, the vizier informed the king, who was amazed and ordered the story recorded. From then on, they lived happily in prosperity, enjoying life until the end of their days.
paragraphs.zh: 他们倾诉着彼此的苦楚，感谢上帝让他们重逢。第二天，首相将此事告知国王，国王大为惊讶，下令将这段故事记录下来。从此以后，两人过上了幸福美满的生活，享受着安宁直至生命的尽头。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far concluded his tale: "This is what happened to the vizier from Basra and the vizier from Egypt." The caliph exclaimed, "By God, Ja'far, this is truly remarkable," and ordered the story recorded. He then freed the slave and bestowed upon the young man one of his favorite concubines, a generous income, and a place among his closest companions.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔讲完了故事：“这就是巴士拉和埃及的两位 vizier 的遭遇。”哈里发脱口而出：“天哪，贾法尔，这真是令人惊叹。”他下令将这个故事记录下来，并释放了那位奴隶。随后，他赏赐给年轻人一位心爱的妃子、一笔丰厚的收入以及自己最亲近的同伴之一的位置。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: In the tale, Al-Misri refers to the vizier from Egypt, while al-Basri is the vizier from Basra. The capital of Egypt, located near the pyramids on the Nile River, was then as it is now a significant city. In some parts of the Middle East, it was customary to present the bride in various dresses to her groom.
paragraphs.zh: 在故事中，阿勒米斯里指的是埃及的 vizier（宰相），而阿勒巴苏里则是巴士拉的 vizier。位于尼罗河畔、靠近金字塔的埃及首都，当时和现在一样是一座重要的城市。在中东的一些地区，有为新娘穿上不同服饰展示给新郎的传统。

paragraphs.en: Damascus, the capital of Syria, was and remains one of the great cities of the region. Situated at the southwestern corner of the Arabian peninsula, it was home to Homs, Hama, Aleppo, and other important cities. Further north, Dyarbakir and Mardin were then as they are now significant cities in eastern Turkey.
paragraphs.zh: 叙利亚的首都大马士革，自古以来便是该地区的重要城市之一。位于阿拉伯半岛西南角的大马士革，周围是霍姆斯、哈马和阿勒颇等重要城市。向北则有迪亚巴克尔和梅尔丁，这些城市至今仍是土耳其东部的重要都市。

paragraphs.en: The story featured a semiprecious stone known for its bright blue color and mentioned the famous Umayyad Mosque, one of the great mosques of the Muslim world, built between 705 and 714 AD. The market of Damascus, with its main street leading to the Umayyad Mosque, was also a notable feature.
paragraphs.zh: 这个故事讲述了一种半宝石，以其明亮的蓝色著称，并提到了著名的乌马亚德大清真寺，这是穆斯林世界中一座伟大的清真寺，始建于公元705年至714年。大马士革的市场也值得一提，其主要街道直通乌马亚德大清真寺。
